title: Could the `augment() ... is not maintained ...` message print at most once per session, please
description:
## Feature

In situations when we call augment() on an ANOVA model, a warning prints out to explain that `augment()` is not maintained by {broom}. But the message prints out everytime that augment() is called on an ANOVA model, even if the warning message has previously been shown. Would it be possible to ensure that the warning message for a given class of model is shown at most one time in a given R session

```

[1] ‘0.8.0’

library("broom")

a <- rnorm(10)
b <- rep(c("x", "y"), each = 5)
m <- aov(a ~ b)

augment(m)
# A tibble: 10 × 8
< ... snip ...>

# A tibble: 10 × 8
<... snip ...>
Warning message:
The `augment()` method for objects of class aov is not maintained by the broom team, and is only supported through the lm tidier method. Please be cautious in interpreting and reporting broom output.
```

title: tidy.coxph does not exponentiate standard errors when exponentiate = TRUE
description:
## The problem

`tidy.coxph` with `exponentiate = TRUE` exponentiates the coefficient (and the confidence intervals), but not the standard error. This could be misleading, so I think it counts as a bug.

## Example

```r
library(broom)
library(survival)
test1 <- list(time=c(4,3,1,1,2,2,3), 
              status=c(1,1,1,0,1,1,0), 
              x=c(0,2,1,1,1,0,0), 
              sex=c(0,0,0,0,1,1,1)) 
mod <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ x + strata(sex), test1) 
tidy(mod)
# A tibble: 1 × 5
#  term  estimate std.error statistic p.value
# <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
# 1 x        0.802     0.822     0.976   0.329

tidy(mod, exponentiate = TRUE)
# A tibble: 1 × 5
#  term  estimate std.error statistic p.value
#  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
# 1 x         2.23     0.822     0.976   0.329

```

This page shows how to get correct standard errors: https://www.andrewheiss.com/blog/2016/04/25/convert-logistic-regression-standard-errors-to-odds-ratios-with-r/

As against that, Frank Harrell argues here that SEs are not much use for odds ratios: https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/156597/how-to-calculate-se-of-an-odds-ratio. If so, I wonder if it might not be better to produce `NA` in these cases.

title: extend tidy method for mediate objects to mediate.mer objects
description:
## Feature

The method `tidy.mediate()` works when objects are generated from `mediation::mediate()` with base R model inputs, but not when inputs are mixed effects models using lme4. The immediate reason is that this results in output given the class 'mediate.mer' rather than 'mediate'. However, after re-classing a 'mediate.mer' object, the `tidy()` method works fine. Incidentally, the `summary()` method for 'mediate.mer' differs only in the metadata presented, not in the table of terms, effects, etc.

I discovered this while working on a `tidy()` method for 'mediate.mer' objects for the broom.mixed package (see [this issue](https://github.com/bbolker/broom.mixed/issues/124)).

**I would like to suggest that a 'mediate.mer' method be defined that simply passes the result to the 'mediate' method.** This would obviate the need for an additional method in broom.mixed.

There may be additional considerations that i've missed. Or it may be preferable to put a 'mediate.mer' method in broom.mixed simply because 'merMod' methods are also there. But i did want to check here first.

The reproducible example below borrows from the `mediation::mediate()` documentation.

``` r
#> Loading required package: Matrix
library(mediation)
#> Loading required package: MASS
#> Loading required package: mvtnorm
#> Loading required package: sandwich
#> mediation: Causal Mediation Analysis
#> Version: 4.5.0
```

Thanks!

title: Add tidy() method for miceadds

title: Dangerous silent failures due to no argument matching
description:
One example: it can look like you're augmenting `newdata`:

```r
augment.Mclust(Mclust_obj, newdata = df)
```

 while you're just getting the augmented original data because `augment.Mclust` doesn't actually take a `newdata` argument.

`validate_augment_input` is going to deal with this in the `augment` case but this is generally an issue with generics where you think you've passed an argument but it just gets absorbed in `...` and ignored. In general some sort of `match.arg` should fix this. This is especially likely to happen in packages like `broom` that wrap lots of things and send stuff through preprocessing helpers like `augment_columns` or `process_lm`.

There are probably a lot of places in `broom` where we need to check that this isn't happening.

Argument matching would be a good thing to include a `Best practices for developing modelling packages` document. cc @topepo

title: Bug in tests: dplyr::last_col() used incorrectly
description:
https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/f3b8ac1730e3e33eb39eaf54ab1b4d4e0547afc4/tests/testthat/test-cmprsk.R#L39-L52

Fails if `_R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_LOGIC2_=true` is set:

```
Sys.setenv("_R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_LOGIC2_" = "true")
  expect_equal(
    summary(fit, conf.int = 0.99)$conf.int %>% 
      log() %>%
      unname() %>%
      as.data.frame() %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::last_col(1:0)) %>%
      unclass() %>%
      unname(),
    td3 %>% 
      dplyr::select(conf.low, conf.high)  %>%
      unclass() %>%
      unname(),
  )
# Error: 'length(x) = 2 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
```

The issue is `dplyr::last_col(1:0)`. The function is only designed to handle scalar offsets.

I'm not sure the intention of the test, so filing an issue instead of a PR.

title: new tidiers: `sampleSelection`
description:
The `sampleSelection` package implements a variety of selection models:

> Two-step and maximum likelihood estimation of Heckman-type sample selection models: standard sample selection models (Tobit-2), endogenous switching regression models (Tobit-5), sample selection models with binary dependent outcome variable, interval regression with sample selection (only ML estimation), and endogenous treatment effects models. These methods are described in the three vignettes that are included in this package and in econometric textbooks such as Greene (2011, Econometric Analysis, 7th edition, Pearson).

Here are minimal versions of a `glance` and `tidy` method to extract results from those models. I'm not super familiar with the package, so not sure this will work on models beyond the simple two-step model estimated here:

```r
library(sampleSelection)
library(wooldridge) # for mroz data
library(broom)

mod_selection <- selection(
  inlf ~ educ + kidslt6 + kidsge6, 
  wage ~ educ + exper + expersq,
  method = "2step",
  data = mroz)

tidy.selection <- function(x,
                           conf.int = FALSE,
                           conf.level = 0.95,
                           ...) {
  s <- summary(x, ...)
  ret <- broom:::as_tidy_tibble(s$estimate,
                                new_names = c("estimate", "std.error",
                                              "statistic", "p.value"))

  # selection models include an outcome and a selection equation
  ret$group <- NA_character_
  ret$group[s$param$index$betaS] <- "Selection"
  ret$group[s$param$index$betaO] <- "Outcome"

  if (isTRUE(conf.int)) {
    ci <- broom:::broom_confint_terms(x, level = conf.level)
    ret <- dplyr::left_join(ret, ci, by = "term")
  }
  ret
}

glance.selection <- function(x, ...) {
  broom:::as_glance_tibble(
    nobs = stats::nobs(x),
    method = x$method[1],
    rho = x$rho,
    sigma = x$sigma,
    na_types = "icrr")
}
```

title: `glance()` error when using a `fixest` object with only FEs
description:
Thanks for the great package. I'm having trouble with `glance()` when using a `fixest` model with only FEs (no regular covariates). Please see the reproducible example below.

```r
# R 4.0.5 / Windows 10 Pro (64-bit)
library(broom)   # tested with 0.7.6 (CRAN) and 0.7.6.9001 (GH)
library(fixest)  # tested with 0.8.4 (CRAN)

ex_fe <- feols(Sepal.Length ~ 1 | Species, data = iris)
```

`summary()` from `fixest` works as expected:
```r
summary(ex_fe)
# OLS estimation, Dep. Var.: Sepal.Length
# Observations: 150 
# Fixed-effects: Species: 3
# RMSE: 0.509616   Adj. R2: 0.613518
```

However, `broom::glance()` returns an error. I think this also causes `modelsummary::modelsummary()` to fail (which is how I found the error):

```r
broom::glance(ex_fe)
# Error in eval_tidy(xs[[j]], mask) : object 'sigma2' not found

modelsummary::modelsummary(ex_fe)
# Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
```

I believe the expected behavior would be to return a df with missing values when needed, such as what happens with `lm` objects:

```r
ex_lm <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ 1, data = iris)

broom::glance(ex_lm)
# A tibble: 1 x 12
```

title: 'tidy_wide' For when you need more than glance but still want a 1 line output
description:
I frequently find myself in a situation where I am looking for more details that I get from glance but I still want a result that occupies a single line in a tibble. 
I almost always find myself copying this function into projects where I'm using broom with simple linear models i R. I don't know if this is a common thing that others encounter but if so then maybe convenience functions to make 'wide' outputs from glance & tidy with consistent column names might be a useful addition to broom?

```
#' tidy_wide
#'
#' used the broom packages tidy and glance functions to summaries the model
#' reformatting the output of tidy to provide just the estimates and p-values
#' for all coefficients in a wide, single row, format.
#'
#' @param model a model object
#'
#' @export
tidy_wide <- function(model) {
	g <- broom::glance(model)
	colnames(g) <- gsub("\\.", "_", colnames(g)) # NO dots in names! 
        # (my preference not strictly necessary)
	dplyr::bind_cols(
		g,
		broom::tidy(model) %>%
			dplyr::select(term, estimate, p_value = `p.value`) %>%
                        # I find `intercept` is an easier to handle column name the `(Intercept)`
			dplyr::mutate(
				term = ifelse(term == "(Intercept)", "intercept", term)
			) %>%
			tidyr::pivot_wider(
				names_from = "term", values_from = c("estimate", "p_value")
			)
	)
}
```

title: no .resid column with augment.lm and newdata
description:
help page says that with newdata argument supplied, 3 columns are added to the dataset. 

> When newdata is supplied, augment.lm returns one row for each observation, with three columns added to the new data:
> - `.fitted`  Fitted values of model
> - `.se.fit` Standard errors of fitted values
> - `.resid` Residuals of fitted values on the new data

However only 2 are there - no `.resid` column is calculated

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

train <- mtcars %>%
  sample_frac(0.7)
test <- setdiff(mtcars, train)


model <- lm(mpg ~ cyl + disp, data= train)

augment(model, newdata = test) %>% 
  names()
#>  [1] "mpg"     "cyl"     "disp"    "hp"      "drat"    "wt"      "qsec"   
#>  [8] "vs"      "am"      "gear"    "carb"    ".fitted" ".se.fit"
```

So either, we could add a `.resid` column but it implies some calculation or at least the help page should be modified.

title: augment.rqs: original data in wrong order
description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with the augment.rqs function and the order in which the original data are stored in the augmented output. I don't have the time to create a PR with the solution at the moment, sorry.

## Reproducible example

``` r
suppressMessages(library(dplyr))
suppressMessages(library(quantreg))
library(broom)
library(ggplot2)library(broom)
library(ggplot2)
data(engel)
rqfit_engel <- rq(foodexp ~ income, data = engel)
rqmultfit_engel <- rq(foodexp ~ income, data = engel, tau = c(0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9))

ag_fit_engel <- rqfit_engel %>% augment()
ag_multfit_engel <- rqmultfit_engel %>% augment()
### the following should be the same 
ag_fit_engel %>% head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   foodexp income  .resid .fitted  .tau
#>     <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>

#> 5    496.   751.   -6.55    502.   0.5

ag_multfit_engel %>% filter(.tau == 0.5) %>% head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5

## the residuals and fitted values are the same

## the problem is that the augment.rqs orders by observation
```

title: aov tidier doesn't work on mlm objects
description:
There is a `tidy.aov` method, but it only works on aov objects created from objects of class lm. If you run `aov` on an object of class mlm, you get an aov object representing multiple ANOVA tests, but `tidy.aov` only returns information for the first one:

    library(broom)
    fit <- lm(cbind(mpg, disp, hp) ~ factor(cyl), data = mtcars)
    summary(aov(fit))
    #>  Response mpg :
    #>             Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
    #> factor(cyl)  2 824.78  412.39  39.697 4.979e-09 ***
    #> Residuals   29 301.26   10.39                      
    #> ---
    #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
    #> 
    #>  Response disp :
    #>             Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
    #> factor(cyl)  2 398891  199445   74.83 3.551e-12 ***
    #> Residuals   29  77294    2665                      
    #> ---
    #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
    #> 
    #>  Response hp :
    #>             Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
    #> factor(cyl)  2 104031   52015  36.177 1.319e-08 ***
    #> Residuals   29  41696    1438                      
    #> ---
    #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
    tidy(aov(fit))
    #> # A tibble: 2 x 6
    #>   term           df sumsq meansq statistic  p.value
    #>   <chr>       <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
    #> 1 factor(cyl)     2  825.  412.       39.7  4.98e-9
    #> 2 Residuals      29  301.   10.4      NA   NA

<sup>Created on 2020-08-18 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

Worse, the method doesn't give any warning that some of the input was discarded. Ideally, this should work something like `tidy.mlm`, except for the ANOVA results rather than the individual coefficients. In the example, I would expect a data frame with 6 rows, and an additional column named "response".

description:
The `tidy.rma()` function assumes that `x$ddf` is a scalar. See here:

https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/4516a805430fae78fd70a6c0277b92fcce767ba9/R/rma-tidiers.R#L69

That may not be true. Consider the following example:
```
library(metafor)
library(broom)

dat <- dat.bangertdrowns2004

res <- rma(yi, vi, mods = ~ length + wic, data=dat)
tidy(res)

res <- rma(yi, vi, mods = ~ length + wic, data=dat, test="knha")
tidy(res)

res <- rma.mv(yi, vi, mods = ~ length + wic, random = ~ 1 | id, data=dat)
tidy(res)
```
No problems. But:
```
res <- rma.mv(yi, vi, mods = ~ length + wic, random = ~ 1 | id, data=dat, test="t")
tidy(res)
```
results in the warning:
```
Warning message:
In if (x$ddf > 0) qt(level/2, df = x$ddf, lower.tail = FALSE) else NA :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
```
because `ddf` is not a scalar:
```
res$ddf
```
yields:
```
intrcpt  length     wic
     41      41      41
```

The simple fix is simply to remove the `if()` check, that is, change the line to:
```
crit <- qt(level/2, df=x$ddf, lower.tail=FALSE)
```
I don't see how a `ddf` value could be negative anyway (given how the dfs are computed inside metafor).

title: `tidy.emmeans()` does not produce a `term` column
description:
The `tidy.emmeans()` method does not produce a `term` column. Instead, the column name is a term name. This is inconsistent with other tidiers and the `broom` spec, where column names are meant to identity the *kind* of information, and row entries represent the *actual* information.

```r
> library("lme4")
> library("broom")
> library("emmeans")
> library("nnet")
> glmm <- glmer(cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd),
>                        data = cbpp, family = binomial)
> emm.glmm <- emmeans(glmm, ~period)
> tidy(emm.glmm)
# A tibble: 4 × 6
  period estimate std.error    df z.ratio  p.value
  <chr>     <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>
1 1         -1.40     0.231   Inf   -6.05 1.47e- 9
2 2         -2.39     0.307   Inf   -7.78 7.49e-15
3 3         -2.53     0.327   Inf   -7.72 1.12e-14
4 4         -2.98     0.425   Inf   -7.00 2.48e-12
```

I think the behavior should be closer to `tidy.multinom()`, where we get a `term` column and a `y.level` column:

```r
> mod <- multinom(factor(cyl) ~ mpg, mtcars)
> tidy(mod)
# A tibble: 4 × 6
  y.level term        estimate std.error statistic p.value
  <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
1 6       (Intercept)    47.3      35.0       1.35  0.177 
2 6       mpg            -2.21      1.64     -1.35  0.178 
3 8       (Intercept)    72.4      37.2       1.95  0.0513
4 8       mpg            -3.58      1.77     -2.02  0.0437
```

Thoughts?

Currently, tidy does not allow one to compute p values for svyolr objects with variables containing more than two levels. Given that this criterion (models containing variables with more than two levels) excludes most models, it renders this functionality virtually useless. I would like to see this functionality added, as I need this in a tidy object to be able to make tables!

A suggestion, before I show the code below: maybe make the calculation of p-values based on something other than dropterm from the MASS package. title: warn_on_glm2 breaks with method function
description:
## The problem
The `warn_on_glm2` function causes an error for a `stats::glm` object where the method argument has been given a function. From the glm docs, 
for the method argument:
>the method to be used in fitting the model. The default method "glm.fit" uses iteratively reweighted least squares (IWLS): the alternative "model.frame" returns the model frame and does no fitting.
>
>User-supplied fitting functions can be supplied either as a function or a character string naming a function, with a function which takes the same arguments as glm.fit. If specified as a character string it is looked up from within the stats namespace.

and the method vaue:

> the name of the fitter function used (when provided as a character string to glm()) or the fitter function (when provided as that).

The trouble seems to be here, where we test equality between a function and a character.
https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/0f4c1caa8d7c3f7162849c3d892e522a913ed966/R/stats-glm-tidiers.R#L166

## Reproducible example

```r
## Based on the example from the glm documentation
## Dobson (1990) Page 93: Randomized Controlled Trial :
counts <- c(18,17,15,20,10,20,25,13,12)
outcome <- gl(3,1,9)
treatment <- gl(3,3)
glm.D93 <- glm(counts ~ outcome + treatment, family = poisson(),
               method = glm.fit)

broom::tidy(glm.D93)
#> Error in x$method == "glm.fit2": comparison (1) is possible only for atomic and list types
```

title: cmdscale support by tidy.list and glance.list
description:
## Context

I occasionally work with multidimensional scaling results from `stats::cmdscale()`. By default, a matrix of point coordinates is returned, which can be `as_tibble()`ed.

However, if any of the parameters `eig`, `add`, and `x.ret` is set to `TRUE`, or if `list. = TRUE`, then a list is returned with a fixed set of names, regardless of which parameters were set to `TRUE` (so that some named elements may be `NULL`). For example:

``` r
loc <- cmdscale(eurodist, add = TRUE)
names(loc)
#> [1] "points" "eig"    "x"      "ac"     "GOF"
loc <- cmdscale(eurodist, eig = TRUE, add = TRUE, x.ret = TRUE)
names(loc)
#> [1] "points" "eig"    "x"      "ac"     "GOF"
loc <- cmdscale(eurodist, eig = FALSE, add = FALSE, x.ret = FALSE, list. = TRUE)
names(loc)
#> [1] "points" "eig"    "x"      "ac"     "GOF"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-09-12 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

## Feature

This consistent naming convention means that `broom:::tidy.list()` and `broom:::glance.list()` should be able to recognize any `cmdscale()` output _other than_ the default coordinate matrix, with helper functions `tidy_cmdscale()` and `glance_cmdscale()`.

I would expect `glance_cmdscale()` to return the additive constant `loc$ac` and the two goodness-of-fit statistics `loc$GOF` as well as the number of points in the input object and the dimension of the representation space, which can be inferred from `loc$points` (number of rows and number of columns).

The coordinates themselves (`loc$points`) are the primary statistical result, so i would expect `tidy_cmdscale()` to return them as a tibble. Analogous to `tidy_svd()`, it might also make sense to accept a `matrix` parameter that defaults to `"points"` but can also be set to `"x"` to retrieve the doubly-centered symmetric matrix entries, pivoted to long form and using only the upper or lower triangle, or to `"eig"` to retrieve the eigenvalues, with summary statistics like those returned by `tidy_svd(matrix = "d")`.

If the team agrees, then i would be glad to draft an implementation and submit a pull request!

title: ivreg tidiers
description:
The new [**ivreg**](https://john-d-fox.github.io/ivreg/index.html) package spins off the old `AER::ivreg()` methods into their own dedicated library.

The [existing](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/master/R/aer-tidiers.R) `ivreg()` tidiers all continue to work with the new package. But these should be separated from the other AER tidiers into their own file... especially since **ivreg** will become a dependency for **AER** in the next release (see [here](https://twitter.com/AchimZeileis/status/1301454613200154624)).

title: Non-standard column names in emmeans-tidiers
description:
## The problem

When inferential statistics are calculated via asymptotic theory, `emmeans`-tidiers produce column names that do not conform to acceptable column names given in the [glossary](https://www.tidymodels.org/learn/develop/broom/#glossary). Rather than `conf.low`, `conf.high`, and `statistic`, the current tidiers return `asymp.LCL`, `asymp.UCL`, and `z.ratio`.

## Reproducible example

```r
> library("lme4")
> library("broom")
> glmm <- glmer(cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd),
+               data = cbpp, family = binomial)
> emm.glmm <- emmeans(glmm, ~period)
> tidy(emm.glmm, conf.int = TRUE)

# A tibble: 4 x 8
  period estimate std.error    df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL z.ratio
  <chr>     <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
1 1         -1.40     0.231   Inf     -1.85    -0.945   -6.05
2 2         -2.39     0.307   Inf     -2.99    -1.79    -7.78
3 3         -2.53     0.327   Inf     -3.17    -1.89    -7.72
4 4         -2.98     0.425   Inf     -3.81    -2.14    -7.00
```

title: `conf.level` has no effect on rma objects
description:
## The problem

I'm trying to return a confidence interval other that 95% from a metafor object. `broom` has the argument `conf.level`  which the docs state should return a different value for conf.high/low. Instead the argument seems to be ignored.

## Reproducible example

This is the example from the docs, but with the `conf.int` and `conf.level` arguments specified.

``` r
library(metafor)
#> Loading required package: Matrix
#> 
#> Loading the 'metafor' package (version 3.0-2). For an
#> introduction to the package please type: help(metafor)
library(broom)

df <-
  escalc(
    measure = "RR",
    ai = tpos,
    bi = tneg,
    ci = cpos,
    di = cneg,
    data = dat.bcg
  )

meta_analysis <- rma(yi, vi, data = df, method = "EB")

# These are the defaults
tidy(meta_analysis, conf.int=TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 8
#>   term    type    estimate std.error statistic   p.value conf.low conf.high

#> 1 overall summary   -0.715     0.181     -3.95 0.0000774    -1.07    -0.360
```

title: Feature Request/Question: Should augment_columns() be exported?
description:
## Proposal: Remove `augment_columns()` from exported functions.

Hi team!

I naively assumed that `augment_columns()` was an appropriate user-level function as it is exported. It looks like it is actually just a utility function (within the `utilities.R` file) and is instead used "under the hood" by `augment()`.

Given that `augment()` is the appropriate top-level function, I'm proposing removing `augment_columns()` from exports OR if needed as an export for other downstream packages, at least indicating in the user documentation for `augment_columns()` that it is a developer-focused function, and that `augment()` is preferred over `augment_columns()` for package users.

Many thanks to clarification with @alexpghayes and @bwiernik in a [Twitter Thread](https://twitter.com/bmwiernik/status/1428728330061295617?s=20)

title: Broom support for rdrobust objects
description:
The `rdrobust` package does a nice job of implementing state-of-the-art methods for regression discontinuity designs but is not tidy. 

Here's a super-basic tidier. I'm not sure how close it comes to broom specs!


```
library(rdrobust)
tidy.rdrobust <- 
  function(fit){
    ret <- data.frame(rownames(fit$coef), fit$coef, fit$se, fit$z, fit$pv, fit$ci, c = fit$c)
    row.names(ret) <- NULL
    names(ret) <- c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value", "conf.low", "conf.high", "cutoff")
    ret
  }


x <- runif(1000, -1, 1)
y <- 5 + 3 * x + 2 * (x >= 0) + rnorm(1000)
fit <- rdrobust(y, x)

tidy(fit)
```

title: Glance method for geeglm objects fails with unstructured residuals
description:
---

I'm running into an issue where calling ```glance``` on ```geeglm``` objects with unstructured residual covariances no longer works:

``` r
library(geepack)
library(broom)
gee1 <- geeglm(Weight ~ Cu, data=dietox, id=Pig, family=gaussian(), corstr="unstructured")
out = glance(gee1)
#> Error: All elements must be size one, use `list()` to wrap.
#> x Element `alpha` is of size 66.
```

<sup>Created on 2020-08-14 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

I've tested this with both the CRAN and github versions of ```broom```.

If I use the 'old' definition of the ```glance``` method, the code runs without issue:
``` r
library(geepack)
library(broom)
library(tidyverse)

glance.geeglm  <- function(x, ...) {
    s <- summary(x)
    tibble(
        df.residual = x$df.residual,
        n.clusters = length(s$clusz),
        max.cluster.size = max(s$clusz),
        alpha = x$geese$alpha,
        gamma = x$geese$gamma
    )
}

gee1 <- geeglm(Weight ~ Cu, data=dietox, id=Pig, family=gaussian(), corstr="unstructured")
out = glance(gee1)

head(out)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 5
#>   df.residual n.clusters max.cluster.size  alpha gamma
#>         <int>      <int>            <int>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1         858         72               12  1.77   622.
#> 2         858         72               12  1.43   622.
```

title: Check for instances where augment fails from `x` columns in data
description:
If an augment method does something like

```r
mutate(out, .fitted = predict(x, newdata = newdata))
```

and a column `x` is present in `newdata`, things will break because `predict` will try to call predict on the column of data `x` rather than the model object `x`. Should add tests for this and make sure that `dplyr` usage is pronoun heavy.

title: Protect against matrix columns
description:
For `broom 0.5.0` we've moved to `tibble` output for all tidiers. Since `tibbles` are stricter than `data.frame`s, this currently introduces some bugs, in particular in instances where `data.frame` is happy to treat a `matrix` as multiple columns of a `data.frame`.

This is likely to affect users primarily in two ways:

1. Specifying model covariates as a matrix object will now error:

```r
library(broom)
library(quantreg)
#> Loading required package: SparseM
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'SparseM'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     backsolve

fit <- rq(stack.loss ~ stack.x, tau = .5)
augment(fit)
#> Error: Column `stack.x` must be a 1d atomic vector or a list

class(stack.x)
#> [1] "matrix"
```

2. Using `survival::Surv` or `survival::strata` objects. This mostly comes up when augmenting `coxph` or `survreg` models when no `data` or `newdata` is passed. Currently this throws an informative error, although previously it just worked:

```r
library(survival)

fit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex, lung)
broom::augment(fit)
#> Error: Must specify either `data` or `newdata` argument.
```

Luckily, matrix-column support is coming (tidyverse/dplyr#3630) and we'll be able to support this again in the future.

In the meantime we should throw an informative error for (1) above and discuss this in `NEWS`.

title: Question: How should fixed parameters be handled in a tidier?
description:
How are fixed parameters handled in a tidier?

When writing a new tidier for the nlme::varFunc classes (bbolker/broom.mixed#114 and bbolker/broom.mixed#115), a question came up about how fixed parameters should be handled in the tidied model value.

To make this clearer, within the nlme::varFunc() classes, it is possible to fix some (or all) parameters to a specific value that will not be estimated.  The value is part of the model in that it affects the output, but it is not an estimated part of the model.

@bbolker and I are discussing the best way to handle the fixed parameters.  And, he suggested that this is possibly something that had been solved within another `broom::tidy()` implementation, and it would be easiest to use that method where we would have greater compatibility.

The initial method that I suggested was to add " ; fixed" to the term column.  Another method I've used in other packages is to add a "fixed" column.  For this parameter, there is no standard error estimated, so it is not a clear signal if the standard error is NA.

P.S.  This seemed like a better fit here than in the RStudio community board or stack overflow.  If you disagree, I will move the conversation to one of those fora.

title: Passing survey models to broom::glance() with lapply/purrr/anonymous functions produces errors
description:
## The problem

Passing `broom::glance()` models from the `survey` package (e.g. `survey::svyglm`) produces an error (e.g. "object 'x' not found) when the `design` argument of the `survey` models is passed objects by piping or anonymous functions. This is particularly problematic because it means you cannot use `glance` with `lapply` or `purrr::map` in most cases. This appears to be an issue with `broom` rather than `survey` as `broom::tidy` works as expected but not `broom::glance`.

## Reproducible example

``` r
# Packages
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(survey)
library(broom)

# Create example "imputed" data
df_list <- data.frame(z = rnorm(20),
                      y = rnorm(20)) %>%
  list() %>%
  rep(2)

# Turn data.frames into design objects
objs_survey <- df_list %>%
  purrr::map(function(x) {
    survey::svydesign(data = x,
                      ids = ~ 1,
                      weights = ~ 1)
  })

# Fit models
mods_survey <- objs_survey %>%
  purrr::map(function(x) {
    survey::svyglm(formula = y ~ z, design = x)
  })

# Works with tidy
mods_survey %>% purrr::map(function(x) {
  broom::tidy(x)
})
#> [[1]]
#> # A tibble: 2 x 5
#>   term        estimate std.error statistic p.value
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)  -0.208      0.213    -0.975   0.343
#> 2 z            -0.0880     0.212    -0.415   0.683
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> # A tibble: 2 x 5
#>   term        estimate std.error statistic p.value
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)  -0.208      0.213    -0.975   0.343
#> 2 z            -0.0880     0.212    -0.415   0.683

# But doesn't work with glance as
# there is an evaluation issue with
# glance looking for `x` instead of
# elements of mods_survey
mods_survey %>% purrr::map(function(x) {
  broom::glance(x)
})
#> Error in .svycheck(design): object 'x' not found

# At first it looked like a purrr issue
# but is reproducible via lapply() so it
# is not just purrr
lapply(mods_survey, function(x) {
  broom::glance(x)
})
#> Error in .svycheck(design): object 'x' not found

# The issue only appears when the survey
# model's design argument is passed an
# object indirectly (via pipe, lapply, etc.)

# Passing objects directly to design works
survey::svyglm(formula = y ~ z,
               design = objs_survey[[1]]) %>%
  broom::glance()
#> # A tibble: 1 x 6
#>   null.deviance df.null   AIC   BIC deviance df.residual
#>           <dbl>   <int> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1          17.7      19  19.6  23.5     17.5          18

# Passing objects indirectly (via pipe or
# e.g. lapply/purrr) reproduces error
objs_survey[[1]] %>% survey::svyglm(formula = y ~ z,
                                    design = .) %>%
  broom::glance()
#> Error in .svycheck(design): object '.' not found
```

title: In tidy.ergm(), summary.ergm()$coefs will be deprecated soon.
description:
`ergm` maintainer here. Long story short, for reasons I give below, I am planning to deprecate `summary.ergm()$coefs` element, and `summary.ergm()$coefficients` (or `coef(sumamry.ergm())`) will return the coefficient `matrix`, not `data.frame`.

The good news is that this is actually consistent with `summary.lm()`, so it should simplify `broom` code, if anything.

## Explanation

Currently, `summary.ergm()` returns two coefficients tables in data frames, one in `$coefficients` and another in `$coefs`, the latter for backwards compatibility. `tidy.ergm()` uses the latter.

Recently, it transpired that whereas whereas `ergm()` can produce repeated parameter names, `data.frame` objects don't support repeated row names and can, in fact, mangle them badly under some circumstances. I am therefore having to transition to using matrices. Unfortunately, it looks like `tibble::rownames_to_column()` does not support matrix input, so this change would break the current implementation of `tidy.ergm()`.

Since I am breaking it anyway, I want to make everything more consistent with `summary.lm()` output, and so my plan is:

1. `summary.ergm()$coefficients` will be a matrix in the next release (just submitted to CRAN). This does not affect broom.
2. `summary.ergm()$coefs` remain a data frame to keep `broom` and other packages going, but will be deprecated and removed in the future.

The good news is that the extraction code used in `tidy.lm()` should work seamlessly, since it also uses the matrix in the `$coefficients` element.

I apologise for the inconvenience, and would be happy to help make the adjustments needed.

title: preliminary VGAM::vglm tidier
description:
I should probably test this more extensively/put it in a pull request/etc., but since I just hacked it up quickly I'm just going to post it here before it gets lost in the shuffle.  There are probably a lot of bells and whistles that would be worth considering.

```
tidy.vglm <- function(x, conf.int=FALSE, conf.level=0.95) {
    co <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(x)))
    names(co) <- c("estimate","std.error","statistic","p.value")
    if (conf.int) {
        qq <- qnorm((1+conf.level)/2)
        co <- transform(co,
                        conf.low=estimate-qq*std.error,
                        conf.high=estimate+qq*std.error)
    }
    co <- data.frame(term=rownames(co),co)
    rownames(co) <- NULL
    return(co)
}
```

By the way, it _might_ (???) be worth considering something like that as a barebones `tidy.default` method -- i.e. many packages adopt the convention that `coef(summary(object))` is a coefficient table ...

title: Unintended labeling consequence in augment_newdata()?
description:
This line in the unexported `augment_newdata()`

```r
    if (!is.null(resp) && is.numeric(resp)) {
        df$.resid <- (resp - df$.fitted) %>% unname()
    }
```
has the side effect that `.resid` inherits attributes from `resp`, the response variable.  This includes the "label" attribute, which is used by packages like {labelled} and {declared} to provide labels for variables.  But the label is typically not an accurate label for the residuals.

Here are some examples.

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("ggformula"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("labelled"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("declared"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("tibble"))

# we can add labels using either {labelled} or {declared}

some_data <- 
  tibble(x = 1:10, y1 = x + rnorm(10), y2 = declared(y1, label = "declared y")) %>%
  labelled::set_variable_labels(y1 = "labelled y")

lapply(some_data, attributes)
#> $x
#> NULL
#> 
#> $y1
#> $y1$label
#> [1] "labelled y"
#> 
#> 
#> $y2
#> $y2$class
#> [1] "declared" "numeric" 
#> 
#> $y2$label
#> [1] "declared y"

# the labels persist in .resid produced by broom::augment()

lm(y1 ~ x, data = some_data) %>%
  broom::augment() %>%
  gf_point(.resid ~ x)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/eSdyjUD.png)

``` r
lm(y2 ~ x, data = some_data) %>%
  broom::augment() %>%
  gf_point(.resid ~ x)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/5n4VNhJ.png)

``` r
# similar things happen with labels of other quantities as well:

lm(y1 ~ x, data = some_data) %>%
  broom::augment() %>%
  lapply(function(x) attr(x, 'label'))
#> $y1
#> [1] "labelled y"
#> 
#> $x
#> NULL
#> 
#> $.fitted
#> NULL
#> 
#> $.resid
#> [1] "labelled y"
#> 
#> $.std.resid
#> [1] "labelled y"
#> 
#> $.hat
#> NULL
#> 
#> $.sigma
#> NULL
#> 
#> $.cooksd
```

I'm probably going to write some methods for `MASS::fitdistr` and `fitdistrplus::fitdist` objects soon, but wanted to put this here in case anyone's already done it (or comes looking for it).

Oops. The `MASS` tidier already exists, and this is somewhat handled [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51434417/how-to-convert-fitdistrplusfitdist-summary-into-tidy-format). Still seems to be some room for adding it to the package.

title: Suggestion: in survival tidier, extract strata variable into separate variables
description:
The survfit tidier currently returns all the predictor variables in a combined string, which could be separated into usable variables.

```r
library(dplyr)
library(survival)
library(broom)

surv_td <- survfit(Surv(stop - start, status) ~ sex + pcdx,
                    data = mgus1) %>%
  tidy()
```

This returns a strata column of the form `sex=..., pcdx=...`, see here:

```r
> surv_td %>% count(strata)
# A tibble: 7 x 2
  strata                  n
  <chr>               <int>
1 sex=female, pcdx=AM     7
2 sex=female, pcdx=LP    10
3 sex=female, pcdx=MA     2
4 sex=female, pcdx=MM    45
5 sex=male, pcdx=AM       8
6 sex=male, pcdx=MA      12
7 sex=male, pcdx=MM      42
```

Ideally, these could be extracted into separate columns, `sex` and `pcdx`, which would allow them to be used immediately in visualizations or summaries. For reverse compatibility with existing uses of the survival tidiers, the result could still retain the `strata` column.

title: Support for discriminant analysis (MASS::lda) in broom
description:
Discriminant analysis (DA) is a well-established and widely used statistical multivariate method. MASS::lda (and related: qda, etc.) is probably the most used function for linear DA. However, it is not supported in broom. I think it deserves specific code and implementation in broom since it is usual to pool results from multiple imputed datasets from a former dataset with missing values, for example using mice::pool, which relies on broom::glance and broom::tidy. 

R. Muriel

PD: This is my first topic (suggested by Alex Hayes), so I apologize if this is not the regular way to suggest code implementation. Feel free to delete, change or relocate the message. #

title: Improve categorical variable labels in tidy()
description:
I'd like to resurrect [this issue](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/issues/16). When a categorical independent variable is present in a regression model, tidy() labels it in the term column by smooshing together the variable name and level. For instance, a variable "Cylinder" with levels of 6 and 8 is labeled "Cylinder6" and "Cylinder8".

For some use cases, it would be convenient to split the variable name and level into separate columns. This would make it easier to create custom formatted labels and join extra information, such as the sample sizes for each level, onto the dataframe that tidy() produces. A reproducible example where I have done this is below. 

I don't think that this feature would need to be done by default, but it would be nice to have it be an option (something like splitTermLabs=TRUE ?).

``` r
## Setup
library(broom)
library(tidyverse)

# obtain character list of independent variables in a model object. 
obtain_model_varlist <- function(model_obj) {
    var_list_raw <- unlist(strsplit(as.character(formula(model_obj)[3]),split=' \\+ '))
    # Remove smooth terms (s())
    return(var_list_raw[!str_detect(var_list_raw,'^s\\(')])
}

# Find frequency counts for all categorical variables in variable list
var_freq <- function(data,var) {
  var <- rlang::sym(var)
  print(var)

  if (is.factor(data %>% pull(!!var)) | is.character(data %>% pull(!!var))) {
  return(data %>% count(!!var) %>% mutate(term=quo_name(var)) %>%
          rename(level=!!var) %>%
          mutate(level=as.character(level), # convert to char
                 is_categorical=1) %>%
           select(term,everything()))
  } else {
    return(tibble())
  }
}

# Iterate through an entire dataset and return a dataset with sample
# sizes for all levels of categorical variables
find_all_freqs <- function(data,var_list) {
  all_freqs <- tibble()
  for (var in var_list) {
    all_freqs <- all_freqs %>%
      bind_rows(var_freq(data,var))
  }
  return(all_freqs)
}

# adds term_name field to a tidy dataframe which includes sample sizes
add_termnames <- function(data,term_freqs,var_list) {
  # Regexs to match the varname (when it begins a string)
  varregex <- paste(str_replace(var_list,'^','\\^'), collapse = "|")

  return(
  data %>%
  mutate(term_name = str_extract(term,varregex),
         level = case_when(!is.na(term_name) ~ str_replace(term,varregex,""))) %>%
  # add in frequency counts and labels
  left_join(term_freqs,by=c('term_name'='term','level')) %>%
  mutate(label=case_when(is.na(n) ~ term, # if not categorical than use original label
        is_categorical == 1 ~ str_c(term_name,': ', level,' (',scales::comma(n),')'),
                TRUE ~ str_c(level,' (',scales::comma(n),')')))
  )
}

## Build Linear Model

Mymtcars <- mtcars %>%
  mutate(Cylinders=factor(cyl),
         Gears=factor(gear))

car_model <- lm(mpg ~ Cylinders + disp + Gears,data=Mymtcars)

# obtain list of independent variables 
car_varlist <- obtain_model_varlist(car_model)
# sample sizes for categorical variable levels
car_freqs <- find_all_freqs(Mymtcars,car_varlist)
#> Cylinders
#> disp
#> Gears

tidy_car <- tidy(car_model,conf.int=T) %>%
  add_termnames(car_freqs,car_varlist)

## Plot Coefficients 

# Default Labels
ggplot(data=tidy_car %>% filter(label != '(Intercept)'),
          aes(x = reorder(term,-estimate), y = estimate)) +
geom_point() +
scale_y_continuous() +
geom_hline(yintercept=0,color='grey') +
coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(lineheight=1, face="bold",hjust = 0.5)) +
geom_pointrange(mapping=aes(ymin=conf.low, ymax=conf.high)) + 
labs(title='MPG Linear Model - Default Labels',
     caption='Sample sizes shown in (). Horizontal lines represent 95% confidence intervals.') +
xlab('Term') + ylab('Coefficient')
```
![](https://i.imgur.com/FbSXHyj.png)

``` r
# Reformatted labels
ggplot(data=tidy_car %>% filter(label != '(Intercept)'),
          aes(x = reorder(label,-estimate), y = estimate)) +
geom_point() +

geom_hline(yintercept=0,color='grey') +
coord_flip() +

geom_pointrange(mapping=aes(ymin=conf.low, ymax=conf.high)) +
```

title: Move dots as far left as possible
Update developer facing documentation
description:
Generally needs a lot of work, but two small things:

- use `arg_match()` (imported from `rlang`), rather than `arg.match()`
- don't use `return()`, just end on the object (purely stylistic). i.e.

```r
f <- function(x) {
  ...
  result
}
```

instead of 

```r
f <- function(x) {
  ...
  return(result)
}
```

This should go in the *How to contribute new tidiers* vignette

title: Allow unconditional confidence intervals for mgcv::gam coefs
description:
i.e. splitting #564 into a new issue 

> It'd be handy if we can have standard errors that aren't conditional on the estimated smoothness parameter(s). It complicates the implementation however but everything we need is given by vcov(model, unconditional = TRUE) (and we may want to pass unconditional through so need that as an argument.)

This will require adding a new `conditional` argument to `tidy.gam()` (defaulting to `TRUE`?) and perhaps calculating the CIs out by hand.

Please tag with whatever the relevant tag is, and feel free to assign me, I'll give it a got by copying the code for `glm`.

title: Brainstorm: Tidying GAMMs
description:
Hey @Athanasiamo, following up from our rstudio::conf conversation. You mentioned that it would be great for `broom` to tidy GAMMs, and also a broader variety of objects produced by the `mgcv` package. I don't use GAMs and GAMMs enough to know what to extract from these objects, so it would be super useful to have a brainstorm here about what to extract for these models, and then base the implementation on that.

Tagging in @gavinsimpson as well. If anybody else has common GAM(M) workflows they would like to see supported, please chime in!

Some questions to get started:

- What classes should we tidy?
- What should `tidy` and `glance` return for GAMs? For GAMMs?
- Is there additional info beyond predictions and residuals that we be useful in `augment()`?

Also it may be worthwhile documenting the structure of `gamm` objects to some degree since the mixture of `lmer` and `gam` components requires some explanation.

Feature-request: Add tidy method for car::Manova.
description:
I think this would be great to have. I couldn't find the tidy method for stats::manova() but I presume it would not be too different. A problem with the car::Manova function is that it fails to return the printed data.frame with test statistic results, approx. F-values, p-values. However, a simple solution is proposed [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25898691/extracting-multivariate-tests-from-the-output-of-anova-or-manova-function-from-c). 
```
# create new print function for Anova
outtests <- car:::print.Anova.mlm
# allow the function to return the results and disable print
body(outtests)[[16]] <- quote(invisible(tests))
body(outtests)[[15]] <- NULL
```
This a bit of a hacky approach and am not sure if it goes against the principles of CRAN or tidyverse. I've contacted John Fox, author of the car package. He is open to suggestions, but he did not like my [previous proposal](https://github.com/cran/car/compare/master...ekatko1:master). I am in contact with him to generate a cleaner way to obtain the data.frame.

description:
I intend to open a PR for this issue.

There are a number of tidier methods that do not pass strict tests because default arguments required for strict tests have not been set.  For example.

    check_arguments(augment.factanal)
    ## Error: length(no_defaults) == 0 isn't true.
    ## Arguments data to `augment.factanal` must have default values. Use `NULL` to indicate missingness if necessary.

***Change 1: Add default arguments***

In order to pass `check_argument` tests, default arguments will be added for the following methods and arguments:
- `augment.betareg`: `type.predict`, `type.residuals`
- `augment.factanal`: `data`
- `augment.kmeans`:  `data`
- `augment.prcomp`: `newdata`
- `augment.rqs`: `newdata`

***Change 2: Remove unnecessary strict = FALSE***

Furthermore, there are 4 `check_argument` tests where `strict = FALSE` where as `strict = TRUE` passes (see below).  These tests will be updated to remove `strict = FALSE`.

    check_arguments(augment.ivreg)
    check_arguments(tidy.lsmobj)
    check_arguments(augment.Mclust)
    check_arguments(augment.clm)

***Change 3: Update internal data to remove warning***

Finally, `augment.factanal` currently throws a warning if `data` is specified.  The internal data structure will be updated to prevent coercion.

    library(broom)
    fit_reg <- factanal(mtcars, 3, scores = "regression")
    au_reg <- augment(fit_reg)
    au_reg2 <- augment(fit_reg, data = mtcars)
    ## Warning message:
    ## Column `.rownames` joining factor and character vector, coercing into character vector 

I do not expect/intend of these changes to be breaking.

title: add attributes to objects to document metadata like conf.method, conf.level etc.?
description:
It occurs to me that there is various metadata associated with tidy objects that is not preserved. For example, if we output from `tidy` with `conf.low` and `conf.high` columns, we don't know (1) what confidence level was used, (2) what confidence method (e.g. Wald vs profile) was used ... similarly with lots of options (e.g. `exponentiate`). I don't know what the tidyverse thinks about attributes, but that feels like it would be a simple/natural way to include this information.  

The very simplest thing would be to include the function call as an attribute (that should have all of the meta-data, although in very obscure cases it could lose information [e.g. someone calls `tidy()` with a `conf.level` argument that is itself a symbol, which turns out not to be evaluatable once the original evaluation environment has been discarded ... in this case it would make more sense to `eval()` the arguments before storing them. But maybe it's not worth worrying about such edge cases yet?)

title: Announcement: standardizing column names. Seeking feedback.
description:
Recently I've been looking at the column names in tidy output and I've found a large number of inconsistencies. We'd like to resolve some of these inconsistencies.

Over the next couple days I'll be opening issue threads for `tidy()`, `glance()` and `augment()` column names. In each thread, we'll entertain proposals for renaming output columns. To submit a proposal, please add a comment to the issue thread in the format:

> Current: `converged` / `convergence` / `isConv`
> Proposal: `converged`
> Other notes/comments: `converged` should always be either `TRUE` or `FALSE`.
> Methods affected:
>   - factanal
>   - lavaan
>   - rlm
>   - glance_optim
>   - nls

More importantly, please provide feedback on proposals. We'll be paying attention to thumbs up and thumbs down reactions as well as written comments. In particular, if you are a package maintainer, please point out changes that would be especially inconvenient/breaking.

The goal is bring as much standardization as possible with as few breaking changes as possible. The `lm` tidiers, for example, will not change since that would break too much existing code.

## Legacy columns names

We're also playing with idea of legacy column names -- column names that we'll keep around for backward compatibility, but that will not be acceptable for new tidiers. As an example, we might decide that to use `p_value` as the canonical name for columns containing p-values. New tidiers would be required to use `p_value` but existing tidiers could still use `p.value`.

## How will column name requirements be enforced

Column names from `tidy()`, `glance()` and `augment()` output are currently tested against glossaries (whitelists) of allowed names. These glossaries are the YAML files and are available [here](https://github.com/alexpghayes/modeltests/tree/master/data-raw). They are currently fairly messy and redundant.

title: glance() on survfit() object without confidence interval mislabels results
description:
Running `glance()` on a `survfit()` object which doesn’t have a confidence interval returns an incorrectly labelled results. The standard error for the restricted mean is labelled as the lower confidence interval and the median is labelled as the upper confidence intervals. I’ll supply a PR to fix this, but in the meantime, here’s an reprex:

``` r
library(survival)
library(broom)

l1 = survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = aml)
l2 = survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = aml, conf.type="none")

glance(l1) # OK
#>   records n.max n.start events    rmean rmean.std.error median conf.low
#> 1      23    23      23     18 36.36439        9.854101     27       18
#>   conf.high
#> 1        45
glance(l2) # Wrong names
#>   records n.max n.start events    rmean conf.low conf.high
#> 1      23    23      23     18 36.36439 9.854101        27
```

title: stanreg, brmsfit tidiers are inconsistent with tidyMCMC
description:
I see that @paul-buerkner wrote the method for `brmsfit` objects and I can anticipate some of the reasons he may have done this intentionally, but I'm not sure whether the current format makes sense.

While some aspects (`par_type`, `parameters`, etc.) are related to broader issues with mixed models (e.g., #96), that's not what I'm worried about since there are ongoing discussions about that. Instead, I'm concerned about the "confidence" intervals.

`tidyMCMC` is basically consistent with the general templates: we have `conf.int` and `conf.level` arguments and it returns columns with names `conf.low` and `conf.high`. 

`tidy.brmsfit` and `tidy.stanreg`, on the other hand, use `intervals` and `prob` arguments and return corresponding columns called `lower` and `upper`. 

I would say that at minimum, the inconsistency between `tidyMCMC` and `tidy.brmsfit`/`tidy.stanreg` doesn't make sense. Now I suspect `tidy.brmsfit`/`tidy.stanreg` opted not use any reference to "conf" because the intervals are not really confidence intervals. My opinion is that it would be better to stick with the `broom` norms (using the "conf" prefix) since users should understand the distinction and it is better than breaking any function that relies on the generality of `tidy` (like the one in my package that led me to realize this issue). I assume there are other model types supported by broom using "conf" that produce intervals that are also not truly confidence intervals, but I'm not certain.

But if others disagree with me about the nomenclature, I think it would then be best to change `tidyMCMC` so that someone who is willing to deal with MCMC models in this specific way doesn't have to switch back and forth between naming schemes to support both `brmsfit`/`stanreg` and `stanfit`/`rjags`/whatever else objects.

title: Simplifying Extensions of `broom`
description:
Given the discussion around placing mixed model tidiers in a separate package (see [here](https://github.com/tidyverse/broom/issues/223), and [here](https://github.com/tidyverse/broom/issues/96#issuecomment-232103247)), I had made a proposal to make a lightweight `broom.base` that minimizes dependencies and makes it easier for other package maintainers to import/export the tidy method within their own packages.

I've put together a [version of `broom.base`](https://github.com/nutterb/broom.base) that has the following dependencies

```
Imports:
Suggests:
    dplyr,
    knitr,
    ggplot2,
    testthat
```

Some notes on this process

* Probably the most offensive, I pulled out `rowwise_df_tidiers`.  I did this to cut out the dependency on `dplyr`.  That's probably counter intuitive for a package in the tidyverse, but I was going pretty extreme on the lightweight.  
* To avoid a dependency on `purrr`, I copied the deprecated form of `dplyr::failwith` as an unexported function.  That will need to be credited properly (it was easier to use the `dplyr` version than to work out the symbols in the `purrr` version).
* I removed the dependency on `psych`, which means I had to look up how to calculate skew and kurtosis.  I drew inspiration for these using `moments::skew` and `moments::kurtosis`.  These should probably be credited as well.
* I believe it would be possible to remove `dplyr` from the `Suggests`.  It could be done by either rewriting the tests to use `data.frame`, or to use `tibble` instead.
* There is an issue to [use `tibble` instead of `data.frame`](https://github.com/tidyverse/broom/issues/150).  This could be added to `Imports:` and implemented. The only dependencies of `tibble` and `plyr` combined are `Rcpp` and `rlang`, which is still pretty light weight.
* To implement this `broom` would need some work to make `broom.base` a dependency.
* In a couple of tidiers, such as `tidy.list`, I had to remove `tidy_xyz`, `tidy.orkutt`, etc...things that depended on other packages.  The `broom` package might need to overwrite `tidy.list` to support these objects.

so the major questions are 

1. Is this something you would be interested in pursuing?
2. If so, where have I gone to far?  Are there dependencies you'd prefer to keep? 


A note of trivia: 

Installing `broom` with `dependencies = c("Depends", "Imports", "LinkingTo")`  isn't terrible and installs a total of 21 packages.

Installing `broom` with `dependencies = c("Depends", "Imports", "LinkingTo", "Suggests")` installs 1003 packages.

title: augment() for plm models does not calculate fitted values correctly
description:
Due an implementation of `predict()` for panel models, which I cannot follow, augment() with panel models calculates wrong fitted values. In fact, the values are only wrong for `within` and `random` models as they have individual intercepts. There is an implementation for `fitted()` but that is not exported and it produces strange values (as I think).

I think, we need a work around here. Here is my test file to demonstrate the numbers:

[see below for a pull request for that:
4ce62e7 and 97cb53f should be a new pull request for #73]

```
require(broom)
require(plm)
data("Grunfeld")

# Use lm() of pooled OLS and fixed effects
lm_pool <- lm(inv ~ value + capital, data = Grunfeld)
lm_fe   <- lm(inv ~ value + capital + factor(firm), data = Grunfeld)

# Use plm() for pooled OLS and fixed effects
plm_pool <- plm(inv ~ value + capital, data=Grunfeld, model = "pooling", index=c("firm", "year"))
plm_fe   <- plm(inv ~ value + capital, data=Grunfeld, model = "within", index=c("firm", "year"))
plm_re   <- plm(inv ~ value + capital, data=Grunfeld, model = "random", index=c("firm", "year"))

# calculate augmented data.frame
aug_lm       <- augment(lm_pool)
aug_plm_pool <- augment(plm_pool)
aug_plm_fe   <- augment(plm_fe)
aug_plm_re   <- augment(plm_re)

# Is column .fitted correct?
all(abs((aug_plm_pool$.fitted + aug_plm_pool$.resid) - model.frame(plm_pool)[, 1]) < 0.000000001)
all(abs((aug_plm_fe$.fitted   + aug_plm_fe$.resid)   - model.frame(plm_fe)[, 1])   < 0.000000001)
all(abs((aug_plm_re$.fitted   + aug_plm_re$.resid)   - model.frame(plm_re)[, 1])   < 0.000000001)

# calculate fitted values "by hand"
pred_plm_pool <- model.frame(plm_pool)[, 1] - residuals(plm_pool)
pred_plm_fe   <- model.frame(plm_fe)[, 1]   - residuals(plm_fe)
pred_plm_re   <- model.frame(plm_re)[, 1]   - residuals(plm_re)

# test hand calculated fitted values
all(abs((pred_plm_pool   + aug_plm_pool$.resid) - model.frame(plm_pool)[, 1]) < 0.000000001)
all(abs((pred_plm_fe     + aug_plm_fe$.resid)   - model.frame(plm_fe)[, 1])   < 0.000000001)
all(abs((pred_plm_re     + aug_plm_re$.resid)   - model.frame(plm_re)[, 1])   < 0.000000001)
```

title: Unintuitive/flipped sign of difference in means in tidy t-test tables
description:
The tidy t-test table produces an unintuitive sign for the difference in means between control and treatment groups. Specifically, the sign is flipped, i.e. positive when it should be negative and vice-versa.

This error can be reproduced by:
1. running t.test(x ~ t, data=dataset) where t is a dummy variable with 0=control and 1=treatment
2. applying broom::tidy() to the result
3. writing the tidy table into an XLSX file using write.xlsx()

title: Change in next spatialreg will break broom
description:
You did not respond helpfully to PR: #696 (my last replly to your rrequest for examples below), so I guess the forthcoming breaking change in **spatialreg** https://github.com/r-spatial/spatialreg/issues/18 will also not elicit a helpful response. `summary.sarlm()` has returned `$Coef`, which is being changed to `$coefficients`, so that `stats::ceof()` will return the fixed effects coefficient table. For a short time both `$Coef` and `$coefficients` will be returned, but from **spatialreg** > 1.1-7, no `$Coef` will be returned. The affected line is https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/173f407bf1332525e4c3187f17b11b919ee1fada/R/spdep-tidiers.R#L51. Further, the `*.sarlm()` methods in **spdep** are deprecated, and will become defunct during this year.

A further note that the `"sarlm" class may also be deprecated, as the coefficient table should not be reported for any models including the spatially lagged response, but an effects or impacts table should be reported. This is ongoing work, which we'll work up as a PR when the time comes.

Thanks for getting back to me. I am not convinced by map/group arguments, and without a reprex say using one of the following standard tests would find it hard to think of a relevant context. By dropping names added for good reasons by function authors, potentially important information is lost, I think.

Some (legacy) examples of named estimate components of htest objects - most of these have meaningful names, often recording how the test was applied:

```
library(stats)
names(ansari.test(rnorm(10), rnorm(10, 0, 2), conf.int = TRUE)$estimate)
names(binom.test(c(682, 243), p = 3/4)$estimate)
names(cor.test(rnorm(5), rnorm(5), method = "kendall", alternative = "greater")$estimate)
TeaTasting <- matrix(c(3, 1, 1, 3),  nrow = 2, dimnames = list(Guess = c("Milk", "Tea"), Truth = c("Milk", "Tea")))
names(fisher.test(TeaTasting, alternative = "greater")$estimate)
Rabbits <- array(c(0, 0, 6, 5, 3, 0, 3, 6, 6, 2, 0, 4, 5, 6, 1, 0, 2, 5, 0, 0), dim = c(2, 2, 5),        dimnames = list(Delay = c("None", "1.5h"), Response = c("Cured", "Died"), Penicillin.Level = c("1/8", "1/4", "1/2", "1", "4")))
names(mantelhaen.test(Rabbits)$estimate)
names(poisson.test(137, 24.19893)$estimate)
smokers  <- c( 83, 90, 129, 70 )
patients <- c( 86, 93, 136, 82 )
names(prop.test(smokers, patients)$estimate)
names(t.test(extra ~ group, data = sleep)$estimate)
x <- rnorm(50, mean = 0, sd = 2)
y <- rnorm(30, mean = 1, sd = 1)
names(var.test(x, y)$estimate)
x <- c(1.83,  0.50,  1.62,  2.48, 1.68, 1.88, 1.55, 3.06, 1.30)
y <- c(0.878, 0.647, 0.598, 2.05, 1.06, 1.29, 1.06, 3.14, 1.29)
names(wilcox.test(x, y, paired = TRUE, alternative = "greater", conf.int=TRUE)$estimate)
```

_Originally posted by @rsbivand in https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/issues/696#issuecomment-519646700_

title: Problem with k-nearest neighbor fitted workflow and glance()
description:
Hi,

I’m getting the following error when `glance`ing a workflow whose model specification is:
```
nn_spec <- nearest_neighbor(
    neighbors = tune(),
    dist_power = tune(),
    weight_func = tune()
    ) |>
  set_engine("kknn") |>
  set_mode(“classification”)
```
The error is:
```
> glance(nn_wflow_fit)
Error: No glance method for objects of class train.kknn
```
`nn_wflow_fit` is a “fitted” workflow; its model has been fitted using `finalize_workflow()`.
Consistently with documentation, when I try to `glance` at the unfitted/untrained model, I get:
```
> glance(nn_wflow)
Error: The workflow does not have a model fit. Have you called `fit()` yet?
```

Thanks!

title: lfe tidiers: tidy(conf.int=TRUE) does not work when there are multiple Y responses
description:
With multiple Y outcomes in the `lfe()` model, `tidy(x, conf.int=TRUE)` will duplicate results. This is because joining with the regular coefs with CI data is done with `ret <- dplyr::left_join(ret, ci, by = "term")`, which ignores the fact that CI should have a `response` column too.

``` r
library(lfe)
#> Loading required package: Matrix
library(plm)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'plm'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:lfe':
#> 
#>     sargan
data(Produc)

packageVersion("broom")
#> [1] '0.7.6'

## works
broom::tidy(x=felm(pcap+util~hwy|state|0|state, data=Produc))
#> # A tibble: 2 x 6
#>   response term  estimate std.error statistic  p.value
#>   <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 pcap     hwy       3.05     0.365      8.35 7.80e-11
#> 2 util     hwy       1.52     0.697      2.18 3.39e- 2

## does not work:
broom::tidy(x=felm(pcap+util~hwy|state|0|state, data=Produc), conf.int=TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 4 x 8
#>   response term  estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 pcap     hwy       3.05     0.365      8.35 7.80e-11    2.32       3.79
#> 2 pcap     hwy       3.05     0.365      8.35 7.80e-11    0.121      2.92
#> 3 util     hwy       1.52     0.697      2.18 3.39e- 2    2.32       3.79
```

title: augment.fixest error when explanatory variable is 'x'
description:
Ran into an unexpected bug with `augment.fixest`, which appears to be coming through on the dplyr side. The problem occurs when one of the explanatory variables is called `x`. 

MWE:

``` r
library(fixest)
library(broom)

set.seed(1)
d = data.frame(
    x = rnorm(100),
    u = rnorm(100)
    )
d$y = 5.5*d$x + 12*d$u

mod = feols(y ~ x, d)

augment(mod, d)
#> Error: Problem with `mutate()` input `.fitted`.
#> x no applicable method for 'predict' applied to an object of class "c('double', 'numeric')"
#> ℹ Input `.fitted` is `predict(x, type = type.predict)`.
```
Stepping through the debugger, the problem occurs in the `dplyr::mutate()` call [here](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/master/R/fixest-tidiers.R#L117-L119). Basically, because `x` already exists in the data, that's what **dplyr** tries to predict off instead of the (internal) `x` model object. Should be pretty easy to fix this simply by adding the ".fitted" and ".resid" columns using regular base assignment rather than going through `dplyr::mutate`. 

CC @karldw who has contributed most of the **fixest** tidiers. I'm happy to put in the PR, though once someone else confirms the same error on their machine.

PS. Just to confirm that running the above example, but changing `x` to `x1`, does not trigger the same error.  

``` r
library(fixest)
library(broom)

set.seed(1)
d = data.frame(
    x1 = rnorm(100),
    u = rnorm(100)
    )
d$y = 5.5*d$x1 + 12*d$u

mod = feols(y ~ x1, d)

augment(mod, data = d)
```

title: Tidier for crr does not include term
description:
## The problem
Reference to #971 

Thank you for including a tidier for the crr objects from the cmprsk package. I wanted to mention that the tidy.crr() function accidentally drops the term. As such, the addition of confidence intervals breaks the tidy function, because it joins the tables based on the term.

I believe I found a quick fix using the as_tibble() function and keeping the rownames as the first column. I am not sure if the as_tidy_tibble() has similar functionality. I am including the example code and potential fix below.

Thanks,
Andrew

## Reproducible example

```r
## copy your code to the clipboard and run:
reprex::reprex(si = TRUE)

## Loading libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(cmprsk)
library(mice)

## Creating toy dataset with no NA values
data(cancer, package="survival")
new_mgus2 <- mgus2 %>% 
  mutate(etime = ifelse(pstat==0, futime, ptime),
         event = ifelse(pstat==0, 2*death, 1)) #0 = censor, 1 = Plasma cell malignancy, 2 = death as a competing risk

imputed_mgus2 <- new_mgus2 %>% mice(maxit = 2, m = 2, seed = 1, method = "cart") %>% 
  complete()

## Creating crr object
fit_mgus_crr <- cmprsk::crr(ftime = imputed_mgus2$etime, fstatus = imputed_mgus2$event, 
            cov1 = data.matrix(imputed_mgus2[,c("sex", "hgb")]), 
            cencode = 0, failcode = 1, variance = TRUE)

## Trialing tidy function
fit_mgus_crr  %>% tidy(conf.int = TRUE)
#> Error: Join columns must be present in data. x Problem with `term`. Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.


#Proposed fix
tidy.crr <- function(x, exponentiate = FALSE, conf.int = FALSE,
                       conf.level = .95, ...) {

  s <- summary(x, conf.level = conf.level)
  ret <- as_tibble(
    s$coef,
    new_names = c("term", "estimate", "estimate_exp", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value"), rownames = "term")[, -3]

  if (conf.int) {
    ci <- as_tibble(
      s$conf.int,
      new_names = c("term", "estimate_exp", "estimate_neg_exp", "conf.low", "conf.high"), rownames = "term")[, -c(2, 3)]
    ret <- dplyr::left_join(ret, ci, by = "term")
  }

  if (exponentiate) {
    ret <- exponentiate(ret)
  }

  ret
}

```

title: fixest tidier ignores `se=` argument
description:
## The problem

I noticed that the fixest tidier is ignoring the `se=` argument. This is happening because the hacky test I wrote in `is_fixest_summary` returns TRUE for some non-summary cases (as of fixest 0.8.3 and broom 0.7.5). Because this test thinks the object is a summary (possibly with the user's preferred standard error or dof settings), broom doesn't pass along the `se` argument or any others except `conf.int` and `conf.level`.

I'll try to submit a PR to better distinguish summary fixest objects from non-summarized ones.


https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/1d6897515ecac6f072afe9c67138477e57d8eab9/R/fixest-tidiers.R#L74-L81

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(broom)

res = fixest::feols(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Petal.Length , cluster=~Species, data=iris)
# Wrong result here:
broom:::is_fixest_summary(res)
#> [1] TRUE
broom:::is_fixest_summary(summary(res))
#> [1] TRUE

identical(tidy(res), tidy(res, se="standard"))
#> [1] TRUE

res2 = fixest::feols(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Petal.Length, data=iris)
# Right result here:
broom:::is_fixest_summary(res2)
#> [1] FALSE
```

In this example, the `tidy_summary_fixest` code should have raised an error about being passed extra arguments. I'm not sure why it didn't.


https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/1d6897515ecac6f072afe9c67138477e57d8eab9/R/fixest-tidiers.R#L84-L92

title: Major revision: adding augment and glance S3 methods
description:
I've added two additional S3 methods along with the original `tidy`. Each of them tidies data from a model, but in a different way. The new methods are
- `augment`: add columns to the original data, containing (e.g.) predictions and residuals
- `glance`: construct a one-row data.frame summary, containing (e.g.) R^2 or deviance

I've added a new branch, [augment-glance](https://github.com/dgrtwo/broom/tree/augment-glance) with this change. It can be installed with

```
library(devtools)
install_github("broom", "dgrtwo", "augment-glance")
```

The new vignettes explain these three methods and how they interrelate.

**Before I merge this into the main branch I'd be very interested in any feedback.** While the package is very new, I would like advice from those interested in using it. (For instance, are `augment` and `glance` helpful names for these functions? Do the vignettes make the difference clear? Which methods should be implemented next?)

title: Retaining statistics names
description:
I'm working on an [R package of my own](https://github.com/crsh/papaja), which will provide functions to knit scientific manuscripts.

To this end, I'm building convenience functions that assemble text strings form analysis objects, such as `htest` or `summary.lm` etc. I am considering to use `broom` to tidy those objects. The only thing that is currently keeping me from using your package is that fact that when I tidy objects I loose all information about what the `estimates` actually are (differences of means, means of differences, correlation coefficients, etc.)---the same is, of course, true for other columns of the tidied output.

Are there any plans to add this information to tidied data.frames? I think retaining this information would be helpful for other purposes and programming literacy in general.

An unobtrusive way of doing this would be to simply add attributes to the data.frame from the original object (adding a row to the data.frame would be another possibility). I've thrown something together for an object from `t.test()` to illustrate what I mean (this should generalize to other `htest` objects with some minor adaptations):

```
> t_test <- t.test(extra ~ group, data = sleep)    
> tidy_t_test <- tidy(t_test)
> tidy_t_test

  estimate estimate1 estimate2 statistic    p.value parameter  conf.low conf.high
1    -1.58      0.75      2.33 -1.860813 0.07939414  17.77647 -3.365483 0.2054832

> vars <- lapply(t_test, attr, "names")
> vars <- vars[!unlist(lapply(vars, is.null))]
> conf_level <- attr(t_test$conf.int, "conf.level") * 100
> conf_levels <- paste(c((100 - conf_level) / 2, 100 - (100 - conf_level) / 2), "%")

> attr(tidy_t_test, "vars") <- c(vars$null.value, vars$estimate, vars$statistic, "p.value", vars$parameter, conf_levels)
> str(tidy_t_test)

'data.frame':  1 obs. of  8 variables:
$ estimate : num -1.58
$ estimate1: num 0.75
$ estimate2: num 2.33
$ statistic: num -1.86
$ p.value  : num 0.0794
$ parameter: num 17.8
$ conf.low : num -3.37
$ conf.high: num 0.205
- attr(*, "vars")= chr  "difference in means" "mean in group 1" "mean in group 2" "t" ...

> attr(tidy_t_test, "vars")
[1] "difference in means" "mean in group 1" "mean in group 2" "t" "p.value" "df" "2.5 %"              
[8] "97.5 %"
```

title: unscaled output of tidy() for lm.ridge
description:
Hi,

I have noticed, `broom` returns the scaled coefficients for `lm.ridge` objects. E.g.:

```

library(MASS)
names(longley)[1] <- "y"
fit <- lm.ridge(y ~ ., longley, lambda = seq(0.001, .05, .001))
library(broom)
td <- tidy(fit)
head(td)
##   lambda    GCV term estimate
## 1  0.001 0.1240  GNP    23.02
## 2  0.002 0.1217  GNP    21.27
## 3  0.003 0.1205  GNP    19.88
## 4  0.004 0.1199  GNP    18.75
## 5  0.005 0.1196  GNP    17.80
## 6  0.006 0.1196  GNP    16.99

head(coef(fit))
##                       GNP Unemployed Armed.Forces Population        Year    Employed
## 0.001 1895.97527 0.2392348 0.03100610  0.009372158  -1.643803 -0.87657471  0.10560725
## 0.002 1166.33337 0.2209952 0.02719073  0.008243201  -1.565026 -0.50108472  0.03029054
## 0.003  635.78843 0.2066111 0.02440554  0.007514565  -1.496246 -0.22885815 -0.01475570
## 0.004  236.65772 0.1948539 0.02230066  0.007043302  -1.434886 -0.02473192 -0.04056629
## 0.005  -71.53274 0.1849806 0.02066688  0.006744636  -1.379323  0.13231532 -0.05366319
## 0.006 -314.43247 0.1765137 0.01937157  0.006565392  -1.328460  0.25560068 -0.05811937
```

In `broom`'s code, there is something to extract the scales as well, but that's only if one value for lambda is given. Information about scales is lost for a range of lambdas (with > 1 elements):

```

tidy.ridgelm <- function(x, ...) {
    if (is.numeric(x$x2)) {
        # only one choice of lambda
        ret <- data.frame(lambda = x$lambda, term = names(x$coef),
                          estimate = x$coef,
                          scale = x$scales, xm = x$xm)
        return(unrowname(ret))
    }

    # otherwise, multiple lambdas/coefs/etc, have to tidy
    co <- data.frame(t(x$coef), lambda = x$lambda, GCV = x$GCV)
    cotidy <- tidyr::gather(co, term, estimate, -lambda, -GCV)

    cotidy
}
```

I think, the `if`-statement in the above code should be something like `if (length(x$lambda)) == 1` to catch the case of only one value for lambda (not a range with 2 or more values). There does not seem to exist a value/vector `x2` in an lm.ridge object (`x$x2`). Also: Do we need to extract the column means (`x$xm`)? That is also only done for the case #(lambda range) == 1.

As I am new to ridge regression, I am not sure if the scaled or unscaled coefficients should be returned by broom. However, given that coef(lm.ridge_object) returns the unscaled coefficients (with lambda=0 you get the (unscaled) OLS estimates), I think broom should return the unscaled ones too?

[Also there is a NULL in code line 36 in ridgelm_tidiers.R.]

title: warn user if lm() produced coefficents with NA (ill-specified model)
description:
If an ill-specified model, in this case with linear dependend columns, is estimated by `lm()`, `lm()` will just drop the respective coefficient for estimation and return `NA` as the estimate for that coefficient. Thus, the user should notice his mistake. If the user does not look at the raw output of `lm()` (or `summary(lm_object)` or has a skript running, he gets no notification (the script is likely to fail at some other point). If one uses uses `broom::tidy()` (without looking at the original output of `lm()`, as I do often, because I like the layout), the ill-specified model is somehow hidden from the users.

Can we have a warning for such cases?

See the example below for `lm()` and also for `plm()` (from package `plm`):

```
library(plm)
data(Grunfeld, package="plm")
pGrunfeld <- pdata.frame(Grunfeld, index = c("firm", "year"), drop.index = F)

# make a duplicate column (i.e. a linear dependend column)
Grunfeld$capital2 <- Grunfeld$capital 
pGrunfeld$capital2 <- pGrunfeld$capital

# lm model
mod_lm <- lm(inv ~ value + capital + capital2, data=Grunfeld)
mod_lm # NA coefficent is displayed
broom::tidy(mod_lm) # NA coefficient is silently dropped, user is not aware of his mistake

# plm model
mod_plm <- plm(inv ~ value + capital + capital2, data=pGrunfeld, model="pooling")
mod_plm # NA is not displayed
broom::tidy(mod_plm) # fails (outside of broom), which is somehow good as the user gets notified about the ill-specified model
```
