title: Suppress "Waiting for profiling to be done..." message when asking for CIs in tidy()
description:
---

When trying to tidy a MASS:polr() model with a single predictor, I get the error message 

> "Error in `colnames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("conf.low", "conf.high")) : attempt to set 'colnames' on an object with less than two dimensions"

This only happens when specifying the conf.int = TRUE option.

Example below

```r
library(foreign)
library(MASS)
library(broom)

dat <- read.dta("https://stats.idre.ucla.edu/stat/data/ologit.dta")
m <- polr(apply ~ pared, data = dat, Hess=TRUE)
tidy_or <- tidy(m, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

Error in `colnames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("conf.low", "conf.high")) : 
  attempt to set 'colnames' on an object with less than two dimensions
```

title: Bug for one-dimensional models in `tidy.Mclust()`
description:
When using `tidy.Mclust()` with one-dimensional models, the mean of each component is given in different columns, and all of them reported in the row corresponding to the last component, while the values for the other rows are filled filled with NAs.

If the model is one-dimensional, there should be only one `mean` column with the mean value for each component.

```r
library(dplyr) 
library(mclust)
set.seed(27)

centers <- tibble::tibble(
  cluster = factor(1:3), 
  num_points = c(100, 150, 50),  # number points in each cluster
  x1 = c(5, 0, -3),              # x1 coordinate of cluster center
)

points <- centers %>%
  mutate(
    x1 = purrr::map2(num_points, x1, rnorm)
  ) %>% 
  select(-num_points, -cluster) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(x1)

m <- mclust::Mclust(points)

tidy(m)

#># A tibble: 3 x 7
#>  component  size proportion variance mean.1  mean.2 mean.3
#>      <int> <int>      <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#>1         1    47      0.167     1.02  NA    NA       NA   
#>2         2   153      0.499     1.02  NA    NA       NA   
#>3         3   100      0.333     1.02  -3.18  0.0961   5.03
```
Expected output would be:
```r
#># A tibble: 3 x 5
#>  component  size proportion variance    mean
#>     <int> <int>      <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
#>1         1    47      0.167     1.02 -3.18  
#>2         2   153      0.499     1.02  0.0961
#>3         3   100      0.333     1.02  5.03 
```

title: Announcement: The State of Broom
description:
My internship with RStudio ends this Friday. I'll still be around (in fact, I'll take over as broom maintainer from Dave with the next release), but will have much less time to devote to broom development since I'll be in grad school.

Here's a list of the current long term goals for `broom`:

- Standardize columns names (#452, #453, #454, #455)
- Improve documentation
    - Consistent argument documentation
    - Consistent return documentation
- Develop additional strict tests in the [`modeltests`](https://github.com/alexpghayes/modeltests) package
- Get the current tidiers to pass the existing strict tests
- Rewrite the core augment logic
    - Meet specifications of modeltests tests
    - Deal with missing data better
    - Potentially move to separate backend for consistent `predict()` wrappers (topepo/parsnip#41)
- Use the `modelgenerics` package (about to renamed)
- Split broom into small domain specific packages (low priority atm)
    - Documentation on how use these
    - Coordinate with other package that implement tidying methods

We'd also like to be as consistent as possible with other `tidymodels` packages.

**If you would like to take one of these projects on** and shepherd it along, please comment here!

title: tidy.survreg function fails when robust = T in survreg model
description:
Error when using robust regression in survreg. I think the issue is that robust regression gives a summary table with an extra column (called "(Naive SE)"). 

```r
fmla <- as.formula(paste("Surv(time, status) ~ ","karno + age" ))
fit <- survreg(formula = fmla, data = veteran, dist = "lognormal", robust = T)
broom::tidy(fit)

summary(fit)$table
```

I propose changing the tidy.survreg function as follows to fix this error

```r
  tidy.survreg <- function(x, conf.level = .95, conf.int = FALSE, ...) {
  s <- summary(x)
  # add extra column name here
  nn <- c("estimate", "std.error", "(Naive SE)", "statistic", "p.value")
  ret <- fix_data_frame(s$table, newnames = nn)
  
  if(conf.int){
    # add confidence interval
    ci <- stats::confint(x, level = conf.level)
    colnames(ci) <- c("conf.low", "conf.high")
    ci <- fix_data_frame(ci)
    ret <- as_tibble(merge(ret, ci, all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE))
  }
  
  ret
  }
```

title: Broom support for spatial econometrics models
description:
Hi,
Would it be possible to allow broom package to be able to work with spatial econometrics model - similiar to models from ```lm``` function

Example is down below:
```
library(splm)
library(plm)

data(Produc, package="plm")
data(usaww)

Produc <- pdata.frame(Produc, index = c("state", "year"))


usaww<- mat2listw(usaww, style="W") 


Produc$slagUnemp <- slag(Produc$unemp, listw = usaww)


durbin <- spml(gsp~unemp + slagUnemp, 
               data=Produc, listw=usaww,  effect = "twoways", model="within", lag=TRUE, spatial.error = "none", quiet = FALSE)
spem  <- spml(gsp ~ unemp + slagUnemp, 
              data=Produc, listw=usaww,  effect = "twoways", model="within", lag=FALSE, spatial.error = "b", quiet = FALSE)

summary(spem)
summary(durbin)

# Augment function not working fot these models
broom::augment(spem)
```
Since spatial models are being use more often I think it would be cool if ```broom``` would support them as well.

title: tidy() ignores ddf argument
description:
Function `tidyr()` ignores `ddf` argument, used to adjust denominator degrees of freedom for interval estimates.

Reference: "HINTS 5 Cycle 3 Survey Overview & Data Analysis Recommendations.pdf"
Contained in https://hints.cancer.gov/dataset/HINTS5_Cycle3_SAS_03112020.zip

```r
library(dplyr)
library(broom)
library(srvyr)
library(survey)
library(haven)
options(digits = 4)
edu_lbl <- c("Less than high school", "12 years or completed high school",
             "Some college", "College graduate or higher")
download.file("https://hints.cancer.gov/dataset/HINTS5_Cycle3_SAS_03112020.zip",
              "HINTS5_Cycle3_SAS_03112020.zip")
hints5_3_rep <- read_sas(unz("HINTS5_Cycle3_SAS_03112020.zip",
                             "hints5_cycle3_public.sas7bdat")) %>% 
  mutate(gender = factor(GenderC, 1:2, c("Male", "Female")),
         edu = case_when(Education %in% 1:2 ~ 1,
                         Education == 3     ~ 2,
                         Education %in% 4:5 ~ 3,
                         Education %in% 6:7 ~ 4,
                         TRUE ~ NA_real_)) %>% 
  mutate_at("edu", factor, 1:4, edu_lbl) %>% 
  mutate_at("SeekCancerInfo", factor, 2:1, c("No", "Yes")) %>% 
  as_survey_rep(weights = "TG_all_FINWT0",
                repweights = paste0("TG_all_FINWT", 1:50),
                type = "JK1", scale = 49/50, mse = TRUE)

model01 <- svyglm(SeekCancerInfo ~ gender + edu, hints5_3_rep, 
                  family = "quasibinomial")
model01$df.residual # 45, ddf for estimates should be adjusted to 49
exp(confint(model01, ddf = 49)) # these are the correct results
# see page 18 of recommendations document and survey::confint.svyglm
# results are same; ddf argument not passed to tidy()
tidy(model01, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE, ddf = 49)
tidy(model01, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
```

title: lavaan update breaks glance.lavaan
description:
The glance.lavaan() function (in R/lavaan-tidiers.R) is accessing internal slots of a fitted lavaan object to extract some information, instead of using the extractor functions. As the internal slots will change in the next update, this breaks the glance.lavaan() function.

The urgent issue is line 136

```r
converged = x@Fit@converged
```
which should be replaced by

```r
converged = lavInspect(x, "converged")
```
as the 'Fit' slot is going to be removed.

But I would suggest changing the whole tibble section to this:

```r
tibble(
    converged = lavInspect(x, "converged"),
    estimator = lavInspect(x, "options")$estimator,
    ngroups = lavInspect(x, "ngroups"),
    missing_method = lavInspect(x, "options")$missing,
    nobs = sum(purrr::accumulate(lavInspect(x, "nobs"), sum)),
    norig = sum(purrr::accumulate(lavInspect(x, "norig"), sum)),
    nexcluded = norig - nobs
)
```
avoiding any access to internal slots.

Finally, I don't understand why the purrr::accumulate() function is needed. I believe that what is intended is simply:

```r
nobs = sum(lavInspect(x, "nobs"),
norig = sum(lavInspect(x, "norig"),
nexcluded = norig - nobs
```
taking the sum over the (possibly multiple) groups.

Yves.

title: `object 'fstatistic' not found` when model contains intercept only
description:
In trying to solve <https://github.com/stefvanbuuren/mice/issues/237> I found that `broom 0.7.0.9000` produces an expected result when the model contains only an intercept.

```r
library(broom)

# normal operation
fit1 <- lm(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars)
glance(fit1)

# intercept only throws error: Error in eval_tidy(xs[[j]], mask) : object 'fstatistic' not found
fit0 <- lm(mpg ~ 1, data = mtcars)
glance(fit0)
```

Is this normal behaviour?

title: Add Standard Error for `optim()`, if Hessian is available
description:
It would be helpful if `tidy_optim()` supported summarizing the Hessian, if present.

``` r
library(broom)

tidy_optim <- function(x, ...) {
  if (is.null(names(x$par))) {
    names(x$par) <- paste0("parameter", seq_along(x$par))
  }
  ret <- tibble(parameter = names(x$par), value = unname(x$par))
  if ("hessian" %in% names(x)) {
    ret$std.error <- sqrt(diag(solve(x$hessian)))
  }
  ret
}

r <- function(x) (3 - x[1])^2 + 4 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2

res <- optim(1:2, r)
tidy_optim(res)
#> Error in tibble(parameter = names(x$par), value = unname(x$par)): could not find function "tibble"

resH <- optim(1:2, r, hessian=TRUE)
tidy_optim(resH)
#> Error in tibble(parameter = names(x$par), value = unname(x$par)): could not find function "tibble"
```

title: Documentation approach
description:
Many of the tidiers return the same type of information about different model types. For example, a bajillion `glance` methods return a tibble with an `AIC` column.

Ideally, I'd like to document what the `AIC` column represents in a single place, so that all those glance methods benefit from the same documentation and there's no need to copy-paste any changes to the description.

Currently, most methods document the return value with something like:

```r
#' @rdname betareg_tidiers
#'
#' @return `glance` returns a one-row tibble with columns:
#'   \item{pseudo.r.squared}{the deviance of the null model}
#'   \item{logLik}{the data's log-likelihood under the model}
#'   \item{AIC}{the Akaike Information Criterion}
#'   \item{BIC}{the Bayesian Information Criterion}
#'   \item{df.residual}{residual degrees of freedom}
#'   \item{df.null}{degrees of freedom under the null}
#'
#' @seealso [glance()]
#' @export
glance.betareg <- function(x, ...) {
  ...
}
```

I'd like to replace this with something along the lines of

```r
#' @rdname betareg_tidiers
#'
#' @template glance_boilerplate
#' @return A one-row tibble with columns:
#'   -`pseudo.r.squared`
#'   -`logLik`
#'   -`AIC`
#'   -`BIC`
#'   -`df.residual`
#'   -`df.null`
#'
#' @seealso [output_column_glossary()], [glance()]
#' @export
glance.betareg <- function(x, ...) {
  ...
}
```

where somewhere in the boilerplate describes how to use `filter(column_glossary, used_by == "betareg")` to get see the descriptions of the return columns.

@dgrtwo thoughts?

title: Broom support for Fixed effect Logit
description:
Hi,

I think it would be cool to add ```broom``` package support for fixed effect logit model from ```broom``` package.

Example is here:
```
library(bife)
dataset <- psid

logit <- glm(LFP ~ I(AGE^2) + log(INCH) + KID1 + KID2 + KID3 + factor(TIME), data = dataset, family = "binomial")
mod <- bife(LFP ~ I(AGE^2) + log(INCH) + KID1 + KID2 + KID3 + factor(TIME) | ID, dataset)

summary(logit)
summary(mod)

broom::augment(mod)
```

description:
Broom is fantastic, really great work! Thanks so much.

It would be great of broom's tidy(), glance() and augment() worked for spatial models. The three I have in mind are the spatial lag model created with lagsarlm(), and the spatial error model created with errorsarlm() in the spdep package. Also, gwr() models created with the spgwr package would a nice addition to broom's functionality. Although gwr() creates a new set of SpatialPolygonsDataFrame or a SpatialPointsDataFrame which is really similar to what augment() would do.

Although I've read a bunch of posts on github, this is my first github request. So please let me know if this isn't the best way to make a request, or if my etiquette stinks.

Thanks again for a great package, its so useful!

title: Spatial Models base function created
description:
Hi,
I added issue on January to add spatial model to broom package.  I write base function myself taking inspiration from broom package codes: I thought I would send them so maybe in future Broom can support spatial models as well.

Function:

```
# This function takes spatial model object and creates dataframe from it.
# Simillar as broom package

tidy_spatial <- function(x) {
  ret <- tibble(.rows = length(x$coefficients), rownames = x$coefficients %>% names(), 
                as.numeric(x$coefficients), 
                as.numeric(x$rest.se), 
                as.numeric((x$coefficients)/(x$rest.se)),
                as.numeric(2*(1-pnorm(abs(x$coefficients/x$rest.se)))))
  colnames(ret) <- c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "z_value", "p.value")
  
  if (is.null(x$lambda) == T) {
    ret2 =
      tibble(
        "rho",
        as.numeric(x$rho),
        as.numeric(x$rho.se),
        as.numeric((x$rho)/x$rho.se),
        as.numeric(2*(1-pnorm(abs(x$rho/x$rho.se)))))
    colnames(ret2) <- c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "z_value", "p.value")
    ret = rbind(ret, ret2)
    return(ret)
  }
  
  else  {
    ret2 =
      tibble(
        "lambda",
        as.numeric(x$lambda),
        as.numeric(x$lambda.se),
        as.numeric((x$lambda)/x$lambda.se),
        as.numeric(2*(1-pnorm(abs(x$lambda/x$lambda.se)))))
    colnames(ret2) <- c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "z_value", "p.value")
    ret = rbind(ret, ret2)
    return(ret)
  }
  
  return(ret)
  
}

# This function calculates overall model Matrics and returns as dataframe

glance_spatial <- function(x) {
  
  #s <- summary(x)
  res = 
    tibble(
      # Using Pseudo R squared.
      r.squared = cor(x$fitted.values, x$y)^2,
      AIC = stats::AIC(x),
      BIC = stats::BIC(x),
      deviance = stats::deviance(x),
      logLik = as.numeric(x$LL),
      nobs = length(x$fitted.values)
    )
  
  return(
    res = res
  )  
}


# This function return Actual and Fitted values from model

augment_spatial <- function(x) {
  
  tibble(
    y = x$y,
    .fitted = x$fitted.values, 
    .resid = x$residuals) %>% cbind(
      as.tibble(x$X) %>%
        select(-1)
    )
  
}
```

and example with artifical dataframe:

```
library(spdep)
library(tidyverse)

data(afcon, package="spData")

afcon$Y = rnorm(42, 50, 20)

cns <- knearneigh(cbind(afcon$x, afcon$y), k=7, longlat=T)
scnsn <- knn2nb(cns, row.names = NULL, sym = T)
W <- nb2listw(scnsn, zero.policy = TRUE)

ols <- lm(totcon ~ Y + x + id, data = afcon)

spatial.lag <- lagsarlm(totcon ~ Y + x + id, data = afcon, W)
spatial.error <- errorsarlm(totcon ~ Y + x + id, data = afcon, W)


broom::tidy(ols)
broom::glance(ols)
broom::augment(ols)

# Spatial models now
tidy_spatial(spatial.error) # Note I account for last parametrs one model has Rho, one has Lambda
tidy_spatial(spatial.lag)

glance_spatial(spatial.error)
glance_spatial(spatial.lag)

augment_spatial(spatial.error)
augment_spatial(spatial.lag)

```

title: Adding n (sample size) as an option
description:
I think it would be very useful to include the n for the model in either tidy() or glance(). Having to add it manually as in [this SO example](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61417205/extract-model-sample-sizes-using-broom-in-r) is a bit of a pain, and the n is often what is needed for an output table. In tidy.lm, this would be a simple, but not sure about the others.

```r
library(broom)

fit <- lm(Sepal.Width ~ Petal.Length + Petal.Width, iris)
tidy.lm <- function(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, n=TRUE, ...) {
  
  # error on inappropriate subclassing
  # TODO: undo gee / mclogit and other catches
  if (length(class(x)) > 1) {
    stop("No tidy method for objects of class ", class(x)[1], call. = FALSE)
  }
  
  ret <- as_tibble(summary(x)$coefficients, rownames = "term")
  colnames(ret) <- c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value", "n")
  
  # summary(x)$coefficients misses rank deficient rows (i.e. coefs that
  # summary.lm() sets to NA), catch them here and add them back
  coefs <- tibble::enframe(stats::coef(x), name = "term", value = "estimate")
  ret <- left_join(coefs, ret, by = c("term", "estimate"))
  
  if (conf.int) {
    ci <- broom_confint_terms(x, level = conf.level)
    ret <- dplyr::left_join(ret, ci, by = "term")
  }
  if (n) {
    ret$n <- length(x$residuals) 
  }
  
  ret
}
tidy(fit)
```

title: lfe-tidier: add argument robust to tidy
description:
`lfe::felm` objects can be printed showing robust/cluster SEs in the `lfe:::summary.felm` with the `robust = TRUE` option, but currently `tidy.felm` does not have that option. Could it be added as an argument so it simply passes through? 

I've tested it on a fork that I can PR (https://github.com/kuriwaki/broom).
``` r
library(lfe)
#> Loading required package: Matrix
library(broom)

# example from lfe::felm help page -----
x <- rnorm(1000)
x2 <- rnorm(length(x))

## individual and firm
id <- factor(sample(20,length(x),replace=TRUE))
firm <- factor(sample(13,length(x),replace=TRUE))

## effects for them
id.eff <- rnorm(nlevels(id))
firm.eff <- rnorm(nlevels(firm))

## left hand side
u <- rnorm(length(x))
y <- x + 0.5*x2 + id.eff[id] + firm.eff[firm] + u

## estimate and print result
est1 <- felm(y ~ x+x2 | id + firm)  # no clusters
est2 <- felm(y ~ x+x2 | id + firm | 0 | id + firm) # cluster SEs


# PROPOSED behavior----
# different SEs depending on the robust option
tidy(est1, robust = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 5
#>   term  estimate std.error statistic   p.value
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 x        1.00     0.0332      30.2 8.60e-142
#> 2 x2       0.525    0.0324      16.2 2.01e- 52
tidy(est1, robust = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 5
#>   term  estimate std.error statistic   p.value
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 x        1.00     0.0329      30.5 8.87e-144
#> 2 x2       0.525    0.0325      16.1 4.94e- 52

# robust = TRUE turns on cluster SEs when those are specified
tidy(est2, robust = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 5
#>   term  estimate std.error statistic   p.value
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 x        1.00     0.0332      30.2 8.60e-142
#> 2 x2       0.525    0.0324      16.2 2.01e- 52
tidy(est2, robust = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 5
#>   term  estimate std.error statistic   p.value
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 x        1.00     0.0292      34.3 1.74e-169
#> 2 x2       0.525    0.0377      13.9 3.21e- 40
```

title: Adding tidiers for regression models not currently covered by `broom`
description:
Here are some commonly used (`class` of) regression models that `broom` currently doesn't support but would be lovely if it does.

- [ ] zero-inflated regression: `zeroinfl` (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pscl/vignettes/countreg.pdf)

- [ ] hurdle models for count data regression: `hurdle` (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pscl/vignettes/countreg.pdf)

- [x] robust regression from `robustbase` package: `lmrob` (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/robustbase/robustbase.pdf)

- [ ] multivariate ordinal regression models: `mvord` (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mvord/vignettes/vignette_mvord2.html)

- [ ] multinomial logit model: `mnlogit` (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mnlogit/index.html)

- [ ] vector generalized linear models: `vglm` (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/VGAM/VGAM.pdf)

- [ ] outlier-robust fit for Generalized Additive Models: `rgam` (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rgam/index.html)

- [ ] resistant regression: `lqs` (https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/MASS/versions/7.3-51.4/topics/lqs)

- [ ] Robust Linear Regression with Compositional Data as Covariates : `complmrob` (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/complmrob/complmrob.pdf)

(I will keep updating this list as I find new, unsupported regression models.)

Unless somebody else does it first, I will also try to do a PR with these tidiers.

title: inconsistent behavior with `mclogit` objects
description:
`broom` currently doesn't support `mclogit` objects. But because these objects also inherit `lm`, the tidier seems to work.



``` r
# setup
set.seed(123)
library(mclogit)
#> Loading required package: Matrix
data(electors)

# model
mod <- mclogit::mclogit(
  formula = cbind(Freq, interaction(time, class)) ~ econ.left / class + welfare / class + auth / class,
  random = ~ 1 | party.time,
  data = within(electors, party.time <- interaction(party, time))
)
#> Fitting plain conditional logit to obtain starting values
#> Iteration 1 - Deviance = 7377.939
#> Iteration 2 - Deviance = 4589.544
#> Iteration 3 - Deviance = 4293.485
#> Iteration 4 - Deviance = 4277.887
#> Iteration 5 - Deviance = 4277.808
#> Iteration 6 - Deviance = 4277.808
#> converged
#> Fitting random effects/random coefficients model
#> Iteration 1 - Deviance = 1876.788
#> Iteration 2 - Deviance = 1212.004
#> Iteration 3 - Deviance = 1009.8
#> Iteration 4 - Deviance = 958.7431
#> Iteration 5 - Deviance = 949.4332
#> Iteration 6 - Deviance = 948.1453
#> Iteration 7 - Deviance = 947.9013
#> Iteration 8 - Deviance = 947.8442
#> Iteration 9 - Deviance = 947.8329
#> Iteration 10 - Deviance = 947.8308
#> Iteration 11 - Deviance = 947.8305
#> Iteration 12 - Deviance = 947.8304
#> Iteration 13 - Deviance = 947.8304
#> Iteration 14 - Deviance = 947.8304
#> converged

# class of objects
class(mod)
#> [1] "mmclogit" "mclogit"  "lm"

# tidier?
broom::tidy(mod)
#> # A tibble: 9 x 5
#>   term                      estimate std.error statistic   p.value
#>   <chr>                        <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 econ.left                  -0.172     0.138     -1.25  2.12e-  1
#> 2 welfare                     2.05      0.214      9.58  9.71e- 22
#> 3 auth                        0.0817    0.118      0.691 4.89e-  1
#> 4 econ.left:classnew.middle  -1.67      0.0880   -19.0   3.61e- 80
#> 5 econ.left:classold.middle  -2.97      0.149    -19.9   4.56e- 88
#> 6 classnew.middle:welfare    -0.989     0.0609   -16.2   2.30e- 59
#> 7 classold.middle:welfare    -1.62      0.129    -12.6   3.82e- 36
#> 8 classnew.middle:auth       -1.39      0.0468   -29.8   1.64e-194
#> 9 classold.middle:auth        1.46      0.0582    25.0   2.05e-138
```

But it has trouble computing confidence intervals because the underlying method from `stats` fails:

```r           
# confidence intervals?
broom::tidy(mod, conf.int = TRUE)
#> Error in qt(a, object$df.residual): Non-numeric argument to mathematical function

# is there even a method for this?
confint(mod)
#> Error in qt(a, object$df.residual): Non-numeric argument to mathematical function
```

The `glance` and `augment` methods also fail: 

```r
# glance?
broom::glance(mod)
#> Error in eval_tidy(xs[[i]], unique_output): object 'r.squared' not found

# augment?
broom::augment(mod, data = electors)
#> Error: Can't augment data with observation level measures.
#> Did you provide `data` with the exact data used for model fitting?
```

``` r
set.seed(123)

mat <- rbind(
  matrix(1, nrow = n[1, 1], ncol = 1) %*% c(0, 0),
  matrix(1, nrow = n[1, 2], ncol = 1) %*% c(0, 1),
  matrix(1, nrow = n[2, 1], ncol = 1) %*% c(1, 0),

gfr <- .06179 * matrix(1, nrow = nrow(mat), ncol = 1)
```

title: Use conf.int idiom when possible
description:
Some tidier methods don't make use of the `broom_confint_terms` helper.

```
  if (conf.int) {
    ci <- broom_confint_terms(x, level = conf.level)
    ret <- dplyr::left_join(ret, ci, by = "term")
  }
```

title: `glance` method fails for `slm` objects
Need to add tidy.speedglm() and glance.speedglm() methods to avoid explosion
description:
There are two issues here-
1. `broom::tidy` works but it converts _p_-values to `factor` type.
2. `broom::glance` doesn't work

``` r
set.seed(123)
library(broom)
library(speedglm)
#> Loading required package: Matrix
#> Loading required package: MASS

# data
n <- 50000
k <- 80
y <- rgamma(n, 1.5, 1)
x <- round(matrix(rnorm(n * k), n, k), digits = 3)
colnames(x) <- paste("s", 1:k, sep = "")
da <- data.frame(y, x)
fo <-
  as.formula(paste("y~", paste(paste("s", 1:k, sep = ""), collapse = "+")))

# model
mod <- speedglm(fo, data = da, family = Gamma(log))

# tidier (note that p.value column is of type factor)
broom::tidy(mod)
```

title: Consistency of emmeans tidiers (with other tidiers)
description:
While working on a [PR to add a new `emmeans`-tidier](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/pull/691), I noticed that the `emmeans`-tidiers have some internal and external inconsistencies:

1. The [`lsmobj`-method](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/57b2400e4df99976f677a1dc360b54793a1232aa/R/emmeans-tidiers.R#L71) uses the common arguments `conf.int` and `conf.level` as defined in the `param_confint` template. The other methods (e.g., [`emmGrid`](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/master/R/emmeans-tidiers.R#L125)) do not provide these arguments and instead rely on the argument names native to the `emmeans` `summary()`-methods (e.g., `infer` and `level`).

I haven't looked exhaustively at other methods, but I additionally noticed some inconsistencies compared to other contrast tidiers, specifically [`tidy.TukeyHSD()`](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/57b2400e4df99976f677a1dc360b54793a1232aa/R/stats-anova-tidiers.R#L265):

2. `tidy.TukeyHSD()` reports the contrasted conditions in a column labelled `comparison` in the form of `a-b`. In contrast, the `emmeans` tidiers return the same information in two columns labelled `level1` and `level2` (containing `a` and `b`).

~~~r
fm1 <- aov(breaks ~ wool + tension, data = warpbreaks)
thsd <- TukeyHSD(fm1, "tension", ordered = TRUE)
tidy(thsd)

emmp <- pairs(emmeans(fm1, ~ tension))
tidy(emmp)
~~~

3. In the `tibble` returned by `tidy.TukeyHSD()`, the column containing p-values is labelled `adj.p.value`. In contrast, the `emmeans` tidiers label this column `p.value` regardless of whether it has been adjusted for multiple comparisons or not (see code above). Unless I missed something, the use of `adj.p.value` is currently unique to `tidy.TukeyHSD()`. 

It seems desirable to try to keep things consistent across methods where possible but particularly within the set of tidiers for a given package. I would, therefore, suggest the following changes, that I'd be willing to implement in a PR:

1. Add the arguments `conf.int` and `conf.level` to all emmeans tidiers.
2. Change reporting of contrast pairs in either `tidy.TukeyHSD()` or the `emmeans`-methods. I'm not sure which of the two is preferable here.
3. Either use `adj.p.value` in `emmeans` tidiers whenever p-values are adjusted for multiple comparisons or use `p.value` in `tidy.TukeyHSD()`. Again I'm not sure which is preferable.

Any thoughts?

title: PCA - Variance explained potential issues
description:
Hi there, I believe there is a minor error in ```broom``` when calculating Principal component analysis - Variance Explained when using Singular value decomposition approach. 

When using broom package to PCA calculated by SVD and PCA calculated by ```prcomp``` function. Proportion of Variance explained is not the same.

I have provided example here:
```
# Libraries -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
df <- iris[, 1:4]


# Doing this "NOT NICE" approach so everyone can see the formula for transformation (line 13)

Center <- 
  df %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "key") %>% 
  group_by(key) %>% 
  mutate(value = (value - mean(value))/sd(value)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = key, values_from = value) %>% 
  unnest()

COV <- t(Center) %*% as.matrix(Center) * (nrow(Center) - 1)^-1 # Calculating Covariance matrix
COV %>% eigen()

PRCO <- prcomp(df, center = T, scale. = T) # Build function

PCA <- COV %>% svd() # Singular value decomposition approach

summary(PRCO)

# Calculating Variance explaned by hand
PRCO$sdev^2/sum(PRCO$sdev^2)
PCA$d/sum(PCA$d)
# Seems that cumulative variances explained by each component are not the same. However,
```

title: Coefficients for ordinal (`clm`) models are listed in wrong order when `conf.int = TRUE`
description:
When tidying data from an ordinal (`clm`) model and selecting `conf.int = TRUE`, the order of the terms don’t correspond to the order of the variables in the regression formula. Instead, they are sorted alphabetically. (When using `conf.int = FALSE`, everything is fine.)

Alphabetical order isn’t *wrong*, per se, but it’s not very useful when one wants to use the resulting estimates in a table or plot and the ordering of the variables in the original formula was intentional.

Here’s a reprex:

```r
library(broom)
library(ordinal)

# Simulate some data and fit a model
sim = function(grsize) factor(sample(grsize, 100, replace = TRUE))
df = data.frame(y = sim(5),
              a = sim(2),
              b = sim(4),
              c = runif(100),
              d = sim(3))
l = clm(y ~ a + d + c +b, data = df) # Note variable order

# Coefficient order corresponds to order of variables in formula
coef(l)
#>         1|2         2|3         3|4         4|5          a2          d2 
#> -2.66579140 -1.49704419 -0.79265546  0.32351718 -0.08526517 -0.88782695

#> -0.56803889 -0.46651308 -0.40220797 -0.59118474 -0.61172131

# Tidying *without* CIs gives the correct order (a, d, c, b)
tidy(l, conf.int = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 11 x 6
#>    term  estimate std.error statistic   p.value coefficient_type
#>    <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>
```

title: Add tidiers for margins and mfx objects
description:
It would be great to have tidy methods for objects from the [**margins**](https://github.com/leeper/margins) and [**mfx**](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mfx/index.html) packages. 

Among other things, this would go a long way towards improving the table support for generalized linear models like logit and probit regressions, where you often want to report actual marginal effects rather than the naive coefficient values. (I'm thinking of the fact that modern table-exporting packages like [huxtable](https://github.com/hughjonesd/huxtable) and [gtsummary](https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/gtsummary) rely on `broom::tidy()` as a first step.) AFAIK, there is currently no fully automated way to produce, say, a LaTeX table of marginal effects from a logistic regression in R.

A potential point of convenience here is that `margins` and `mfx` both produce output that already closely resemble tidied regression output. 

``` r
## Run a logistic regression
log_reg <- glm(am ~ cyl + hp + wt, data = mtcars, family = binomial)

## Tidy (but naive) coefficient values
library(broom)
tidy(log_reg)
#> # A tibble: 4 x 5
#>   term        estimate std.error statistic p.value
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)  19.7       8.12       2.43   0.0152
#> 2 cyl           0.488     1.07       0.455  0.649 
#> 3 hp            0.0326    0.0189     1.73   0.0840
#> 4 wt           -9.15      4.15      -2.20   0.0276

## Get the actual marginal effects instead

## Option 1: margins package
library(margins, quietly = T)
summary(margins(log_reg))
#>  factor     AME     SE       z      p   lower   upper
#>     cyl  0.0215 0.0470  0.4567 0.6479 -0.0706  0.1135
#>      hp  0.0014 0.0006  2.3197 0.0204  0.0002  0.0026
#>      wt -0.4025 0.1154 -3.4880 0.0005 -0.6287 -0.1764

## Option 2: mfx package
library(mfx, quietly = T, warn.conflicts = F)
logitmfx(log_reg, atmean = F, data = mtcars)
#> Call:
#> logitmfx(formula = log_reg, data = mtcars, atmean = F)
#> 
#> Marginal Effects:
#>          dF/dx  Std. Err.       z  P>|z|
#> cyl  0.0214528  0.0499376  0.4296 0.6675
#> hp   0.0014339  0.0014602  0.9820 0.3261
#> wt  -0.4025475  0.3782646 -1.0642 0.2872
```

title: Prediction intervals in augment()?
description:
As far as I am aware, `augment()` always returns confidence intervals rather than prediction intervals. I suspect that people often treat confidence intervals as prediction intervals without realizing it, and wonder if adding an explicit option for prediction intervals might result in catching this distinct more often.

**Aside**: this issue brought to you by an incoming `se_fit = FALSE/TRUE` argument to `augment()` methods so that users can control when to calculate confidence intervals for predictions, as this can be time consuming for some models.

title: Variable names do not match in the contents: tidy.prcomp(matrix = "pcs")
description:
In the results of `tidy.prcomp` (with `matrix = "pcs"`), variable name `percent` is misleading. Documentaion states:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12725868/50937948-ae0c7e80-147e-11e9-9e2d-af6e30803937.png)

I understand "percent" as a number ranging from 0 to 100, and the result is the number ranging from 0 to 1 (i.e., a proporton or a fraction). In the example below, `0.620` is 62.0% not 0.62%. In some situations it is confusing.

``` r
library(broom)
pc <- prcomp(USArrests, scale = TRUE)

#> 4     4   0.416  0.0434      1
```

title: Allow for changing the RMST produced in glance.survfit
description:
glance.survfit (and presumably tidy.survfit) returns a dataframe of summary statistics for a survfit object, but does not allow for specifying the restricted mean survival time (RMST) threshold (which is handled by the print.survfit function in the survival package), and instead only can produce the RMST using default threshold.  

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(survival)

T = rexp(1000, rate = 1)
status = rbinom(1000, 1, 0.6)
sfit = survfit(Surv(time = T, event = status) ~ 1)

print(sfit, print.rmean = TRUE) # print summary stats with default threshold for RMST
sfit %>% glance # matches the above print 

print(sfit, rmean = 3) # different threshold for RMST
sfit %>% glance(rmean = 3) # still uses default threshold
```

title: Make p-value optional in tidy output
description:
`tidy()` conforms to the standard regression output and displays estimates, standard errors, test statistics, and p-values:

``` r
library(broom)

fit <- lm(Sepal.Width ~ Petal.Length + Petal.Width, iris)
tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 5
#>   term         estimate std.error statistic  p.value
#>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)     3.59     0.0937     38.3  2.51e-78
#> 2 Petal.Length   -0.257    0.0669     -3.84 1.80e- 4
#> 3 Petal.Width     0.364    0.155       2.35 2.01e- 2
```

While this is standard, I think not displaying p-values by default, but instead making them an optional argument that could be turned on would be better. Obtaining p-values is not necessarily the purpose of model fitting, so they shouldn't be part of the default output. This would also have benefits from an education perspective as well.

I am imagining the following being the default output for tidy:

``` r
tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 4
#>   term         estimate std.error statistic
#>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)     3.59     0.0937     38.3 
#> 2 Petal.Length   -0.257    0.0669     -3.84
#> 3 Petal.Width     0.364    0.155       2.35
```

And the current default output obtainable with something like:

``` r
tidy(fit, p.value = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 5
#>   term         estimate std.error statistic  p.value
#>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)     3.59     0.0937     38.3  2.51e-78
#> 2 Petal.Length   -0.257    0.0669     -3.84 1.80e- 4
#> 3 Petal.Width     0.364    0.155       2.35 2.01e- 2
```

title: tidy.lm "error on inappropriate subclassing" breaks my code - is stop() needed / could it be overruled by argument?
description:
In psychology research, I often need to compare and display standardised and non-standardised lm models side-by-side. Therefore, I have written a function that returns a standardised lm model, with two classes "lm" and "rN_std." I then use the second class to distinguish standardised and non-standardised models for reporting - however, I would like to use the broom tidiers on both, which worked fine in the spring.

When I now returned to this after a few months, the code doesn't work anymore because of the new error on inappropriate subclassing (#742). I am not sure what the history behind that error is, or whether I am abusing classes too grossly - but I wonder whether the error could be replaced by a warning or whether there could be an argument to ignore extra classes?

title: felm.tidy gives wrong confidence intervals
description:
Following on from [here](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/pull/818#issuecomment-681028890).

### Problem

The current `tidy.felm(... conf.int = TRUE)` method — see [here](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/blob/master/R/lfe-tidiers.R#L70) — doesn't account for cases where `robust = TRUE` is also passed as an argument. In these cases, the CIs will still reflect the non-robust (albeit, possibly clustered) SEs of the underlying felm object.

See reprex below. Including `robust = TRUE` in the second example causes the SEs, t-stats and p-vals to change... but not the CIs.

```r
library(broom) ## Using dev version
library(lfe)
#> Loading required package: Matrix

N <- 1e2
DT <- data.frame(
  id = sample(5, N, TRUE),
  v1 = sample(5, N, TRUE),
  v2 = sample(1e6, N, TRUE),
  v3 = sample(round(runif(100, max = 100), 4), N, TRUE),
  v4 = sample(round(runif(100, max = 100), 4), N, TRUE)
)

result_felm <- felm(v2 ~ v3, DT)
tidy(result_felm, conf.int = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 7
#>   term        estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)  467162.    62514.     7.47  3.32e-11  343105.   591219.
#> 2 v3              449.     1082.     0.415 6.79e- 1   -1698.     2597..

tidy(result_felm, conf.int = TRUE, robust = TRUE) ## SEs, t-stats and p-vals change but not CIs!
#> # A tibble: 2 x 7
#>   term        estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)  467162.    64454.     7.25  9.82e-11  343105.   591219.
#> 2 v3              449.     1103.     0.407 6.85e- 1   -1698.     2597.
```

### Solution

The native way to adjust `confint.felm` for robust objects is to pass a `type = 'robust'` argument. 

```r
confint(result_felm)
#>                  2.5 %     97.5 %
#> (Intercept) 354017.777 576985.126
#> v3           -1405.655   2703.366

confint(result_felm, type = 'robust')
#>                  2.5 %     97.5 %
#> (Intercept) 352036.368 578966.535
#> v3           -1614.732   2912.443
```

Should be easy to adjust `tidy.felm` according. I'll submit a PR shortly.

### Update

In digging some more, I've realised the conf.int = TRUE argument is failing for several other cases, e.g. if passed a mult-response object. I think I've got the various cases covered with the PR I'm about to submit, though...

title: Argument to pass additional summary functions to glance
description:
I'd sometimes like to add additional information to a `glance()` summary table, and it would be nice to be able to do this as part of the `glance` call, rather than needing to `mutate` the data frame afterward. For example, with a linear model, I might want to compute the corrected AIC (AICc) or a confidence interval for `r.squared`. 

It would be nice to be able to do so with a call like this to specify such additional functions:
```
glance(model, funs = list(AICc = AICc))
```

Here is a full example:

``` r
library(broom)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
AICc <- function (object, ..., k = 2) {
  UseMethod("AICc")
}
AICc.default <- function(object, ..., k = 2, n = NULL) {
  aic <- AIC(object, k = k)
  df <- attr(logLik(object), "df")
  if (is.null(n)) {
    n <- tryCatch(nobs(object),
                  error = function(e)
                    stop("Could not determine sample size for `fit`. Please specify `n`.")
    )
  }
  return(aic + 2 * (df^2 + df) / (n - df - 1))
}

mod <- lm(mpg ~ factor(cyl) + log(disp), data = mtcars)

AICc(mod)
#> [1] 159.4323
glance(mod, funs = list(AICc = AICc))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 12
#>   r.squared adj.r.squared sigma statistic  p.value    df logLik   AIC   BIC
#>       <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     0.835         0.817  2.58      47.2 4.47e-11     3  -73.6  157.  164.
#> # ... with 3 more variables: deviance <dbl>, df.residual <int>, nobs <int>
glance(mod) %>% mutate(AICc = AICc(mod))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 13
#>   r.squared adj.r.squared sigma statistic  p.value    df logLik   AIC   BIC
#>       <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     0.835         0.817  2.58      47.2 4.47e-11     3  -73.6  157.  164.
#> # ... with 4 more variables: deviance <dbl>, df.residual <int>, nobs <int>,
#> #   AICc <dbl>
```

<sup>Created on 2020-09-07 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

The output of the two `glance` calls would be the same.

Functions should be expected to return a single (probably numeric) value. Functions with vector output could be accepted by creating names the same way that `tidyr::pivot_longer` does by conctatenating the name given in `funs` to the names of the vector output.

Would you be open to a pull request implementing this?

title: discrepancy between augment's .fitted and glm's fitted.values
description:
`broom::augment()` is not correctly calculating the values for `y = b0 + b1*x1  + b2*x2 ... + e` in the context of a general lineal model obtained with the `glm()` function. It strongly differs with the result from `model <- glm(...); moel$fitted.values`, and I also used Stata to be sure about this and confirmed with a serious econometrician.

---

Sorry in advance the reprex didn't find the rds in the project. Here is a manual copy paste:

```r
library(dplyr)
library(multiwayvcov)
library(lmtest)
library(broom)

# clean the data exactly as in stata ----

d_ols <- ch1_application1 %>%
  # Step 1
  filter(year %in% seq(1986, 2006, 4)) %>%

  # Step 2 and 3

    exporter != importer,
    trade > 0

# model ----

d_fe %>%

d_fe %>%
```

title: Column name '.pred' for prediction intervals?
description:
The interval column names in augment() are always called `.conf.low` and `.conf.high`, regardless of whether `"confidence"` or `"prediction"` is specified for `interval`. I think this is potentially confusing and may be misleading in reports if the user doesn't rename the columns. I suggest changing the column names to `.pred.low` and `.pred.high` when `interval = "prediction"` (cf. in the metafor package, confidence intervals are labeled `ci` and prediction intervals labeled `pi`: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/acacdcaa56ce6ed9c7c3239c15007b14d03012c8/man/predict.rma.Rd#L47).

``` r
broom::augment(lm(mpg ~ hp + disp, data = mtcars), interval = "prediction")
```

description:
We've had a few issues recently about trouble with S3 dispatch for model objects that used to fall back to `tidy.lm()` (or other subclasses), but now error out with `No tidy method for objects of class ____`. 

Examples and reprexes on #939, #947.

Initially thought tidymodels/parsnip#291 might be related (thanks, @juliasilge!), but, ideally, we wouldn't actually be explicitly exporting / directing objects from packages currently not in `Imports` or `Suggests` to the `lm` tidier or others.

title: consistent method description in `htest`
description:
This is minor, but for some reason, there is extra space in the method detalils only when the test is Two Sample t-test:

```r
m1 <- t.test(extra ~ 1, data = sleep)
m2 <- t.test(extra ~ group, data = sleep, var.equal = FALSE)
m3 <- t.test(extra ~ group, data = sleep, var.equal = TRUE)

broom::tidy(m1)$method
#> [1] "One Sample t-test"
broom::tidy(m2)$method
#> [1] "Welch Two Sample t-test"
broom::tidy(m3)$method
#> [1] " Two Sample t-test"
```

title: No tidy method for objects of class rsm (what happened?)
description:
## The Problem
Hey guys,

I am running R version to 4.0.2, "Taking off again", and RStudio version 1.3.1093 (macOS Catalina 10.15.7). I do DoE analysis and I typically like using the tidy methods from the broom package to display the rsm model output summary. I'm not sure what is driving this error, but I'm now getting an error saying "No tidy method for objects of class rsm." I've never come across this in the past. 

Thanks for your insight. 

## Reproducible example

```r
set.seed(28)
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(rsm)

# Simple Test Design from a DoE book..
df <- tribble(~A, ~B, ~C, ~D, ~Y,
                 20, 2, 6, 4, 23,
                 60, 2, 6, 4, 15,
                 20, 6, 6, 4, 16,
                 60, 6, 6, 4, 18,
                 20, 2, 30, 4, 25,
                 60, 2, 30, 4, 16,
                 20, 6, 30, 4, 17,
                 60, 6, 30, 4, 26,
                 20, 2, 6, 20, 28,
                 60, 2, 6, 20, 16,
                 20, 6, 6, 20, 18,
                 60, 6, 6, 20, 21,
                 20, 2, 30, 20, 36,
                 60, 2, 30, 20, 24,
                 20, 6, 30, 20, 33,
                 60, 6, 30, 20, 34)

rbind(
  df %>% map(max), 
  df %>% map(min)
  ) 


test_design <- rsm::coded.data(
  df,  
  formulas = list(
    a ~ (A - (60+20)/2)/((60-20)/2),
    b ~ (B - (6+2)/2)/((6-2)/2),
    c ~ (C - (30+6)/2)/((30-6)/2),
    d ~ (D - (20+4)/2)/((20-4)/2)
  )
)
                                  
                                  
rsm.model <- test_design %>% rsm::rsm(formula = Y ~ FO(a,b,c,d) + TWI(a,b,c,d))
rsm.model %>% summary()

# Produce a tidy summary using broom:
rsm.model %>% broom::tidy()
```

title: consistent column order for `htest` objects
description:
Usually, `broom` follows a definite order for columns: `estimate`, `statistic`, `p.value`, `parameter`, etc.

```r
broom::tidy(t.test(extra ~ group, data = sleep))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 10
#>   estimate estimate1 estimate2 statistic p.value parameter conf.low conf.high
#>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1    -1.58      0.75      2.33     -1.86  0.0794      17.8    -3.37     0.205
#> # ... with 2 more variables: method <chr>, alternative <chr>

broom::tidy(chisq.test(c(A = 20, B = 15, C = 25)))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 4
#>   statistic p.value parameter method                                  
#>       <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>                                   
#> 1       2.5   0.287         2 Chi-squared test for given probabilities

broom::tidy(binom.test(c(682, 243), p = 3/4))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 8
#>   estimate statistic p.value parameter conf.low conf.high method     alternative
#>      <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>      <chr>      
#> 1    0.737       682   0.382       925    0.708     0.765 Exact bin~ two.sided
```

But this order changes for `oneway.test`:

```r

#> Multiple parameters; naming those columns num.df, denom.df
#> # A tibble: 1 x 5

#> 1      1   17.8      3.46  0.0794 One-way analysis of means (not assuming equal~
```

title: augment(..., data = df) fails when df has missing data
description:
```r
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

df <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 2 * (1:10) + 5 + rnorm(10))
df[5, 2] <- NA

lm(y ~ x, df) %>% 
  augment(data = df)
```

The reprex above mimics the one [in this other issue](https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/issues/168#issuecomment-641221590).

The function works fine when there are no missing data, but as soon as 1+ row(s) get(s) excluded for missingness, `augment` fails.

This happened over the last week -- everything worked fine 8 days ago. It looks like it might be related to a change in `vctrs`.

title: Rchoice tidiers
description:
I created a tidier for Rchoice model objects. I am not sophisticated enough to add to Broom, but maybe others can? Here it is below. It works now to call modelsummary (which relies on broom). Maybe someone more R savy can integrate this so that Rchoice objects can be tidied, or whatever you call it. 


tidy.Rchoice <- function(object, ...) {
  s <- getSummary.Rchoice(object, ...)
  ret <- tibble::tibble(term = row.names(s$coef),
                        estimate = s$coef[, 1],
                        std.error = s$coef[, 2],
                        z.value=s$coef[, 3], 
                        p.value=s$coef[,4],
                        conf.low=s$coef[,5],
                        conf.high=s$coef[,6])
  ret
}
glance.Rchoice <- function(object, ...) {
  s <- getSummary.Rchoice(object, ...)
  ret <- tibble::tibble(
                        n = s$sumstat['N'],
                        logLik = s$sumstat['logLik'],
                        AIC = s$sumstat['AIC'],
                        BIC = s$sumstat['BIC'],
                        df = s$sumstat['df']
                        )
  ret
}

title: Glance in a linear regression without intercept
description:
I was running a simple linear regression without a intercept:

`regression <-lm (y ~ x + 0, data=data)`

But when I tried to pass the output to tidy:

`glance (regression)`

This didn't return a value for F-Statistic, p-value or df (only returns r.squared, adj.r.squared, sigma, logLik, AIC, BIC, deviance and df.residual).

But when I used the tradicional:

`summary (regression)`

It shows values for those 3 (F-Statistic, p-value or df ).

And when I runned with a intercept:

`regression <-lm (y ~ x + 1, data=data)`

`glance (regression)` returns all.


Thanks in advance.

title: Use exponentiate idiom when possible
coxph with frailty models fails when conf.int=TRUE
description:
Hi, thank you for the great work on the broom package

I'am using CRAN broom 0.7.0

I'am triyng a coxph model with a frailty term. When using tidy without conf.int = TRUE, everything works properly 

```r
library(survival)
library(broom)

model <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + frailty(inst), lung)
tidy(model, conf.int = FALSE)
```

But when using conf.int = TRUE, it returns an errors 
```r
model <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + frailty(inst), lung)
tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE)
```

Note that if your coxphmodel only has one variable, the confidence interval will recycle when the function binds the conf int with the coefficients.
```r
model <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + frailty(inst), lung)
tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE)
```

I guess the conf.int should be [NA-NA] for the frailty term ?
I may be able to contribute a solution but I'am not very used to github...
Kind regards

title: add tidier for competing risks results `crr` class from `cmprsk` package
description:
---

My colleagues and I use competing risks models often and the results seem to be ripe for a tidier! 

I have started working on the problem, using the survival-coxph-tidiers as a template since the results are quite similar. 

I would be happy to work on this issue - are there any other competing risks models that people commonly like to use?

 
``` r
library(cmprsk)
#> Loading required package: survival
set.seed(2)
#time to loco-regional failure (lrf)
lrf_time <- rexp(100)

# Event 0 = censored, 1 = LRF w/ or w/o death, 2 = Death w/o LRF
lrf_event <- sample(0:2, 100, replace = TRUE) 

# Treatment vs placebo or something
trt <- sample(0:1, 100, replace = TRUE)

# Another variable
strt <- sample(1:2, 100, replace = TRUE)

#make competing risks model 
mod_crr <- crr(lrf_time, lrf_event, cbind(trt, strt))

# very tidy-able summary of coefficients
cmprsk::summary.crr(mod_crr)$coef
#>             coef exp(coef)  se(coef)          z p-value

#> strt -0.04375598 0.9571875 0.3876434 -0.1128769    0.91
```

title: Laundry list of tidy argument / behavioral consistency items
description:
Based on looking at the non-standard arguments to `tidy` methods.

- [x] `tidy.boot`: document that `conf.method` is passed to `boot::boot.ci(..., type = conf.method)`
- [ ] `tidy.brmsfit`. Rename `intervals = conf.int`, `prob = conf.level`, decide what to do with `parameters`
- [x] `tidy.felm` example returns NaN rather than NA. Remove `fe.error`, only use `fe`. Possibly rename to `include_fe`
- [ ] Document that undefined / unknown values should **always** be `NA`. Test for `Inf` and `NaN`.
- [ ] New tidier vignette: written documentation should default argument values
- [ ] New tidier vignette: document behavior when `data`/`newdata`/neither is provided
- [ ] `tidy.gam`: `parametric` currently a switch. should parametric always be returned, with non-parametric return optionally? Or should they both always be returned (leaning toward this). Ask Gavin.
- [ ] `tidy.kmeans`: rename `col.names` arg
- [x] `tidy.manova` doc: specify what `test` gets passed to. perhaps rename `test` to `method`, which is used elsewhere
- [ ] `tidy.prcomp` doc: rename `matrix` arg?
- [x] harmonize `diag` and `diagonal` across `tidy.dist` and `tidy.rcorr`
- [ ] `tidy.rjags`: `pars` consistency with other parameter type arguments. rename `estimate.method`?
- [ ] `tidy.rq/tidy.rqs`: rename `se.type` since everywhere else it's `std.error`. Remove `alpha` arg and use `conf.level` instead, inverting or whatever is necessary to translate between scales
- [ ] `tidy.stanfit`: remove `droppars`, redundant with `pars`. rename `rhat, ess` to `include_rhat, include_ess`? or just include these by default. I'm a fan of `tidy` giving you lots of stuff that you can then `select(-stuff)` away immediately after if you don't want it.
- [ ] `tidy.stanreg`: Decide on `parameters`, see below. Rename `intervals = conf.int`, `prob = conf.level`. #291.
- [x] `tidy.TukeyHSD`: remove `separate.levels` argument and allow user to call `dplyr::separate` later if they want. This is consistent with the `multcomp::glht` tidier behavior.

## Parameter selection in bayesian and hierarchical models

Currently arguments `pars`, `parameters`, `droppars` accept:

- a categorical choice defining which type of tidier to return
- a regex for a parameter names
- raw parameter names, etc

Regex/raw parameter names are ugly and make the user do the work. We should either do the work for the user with a `tidyselect`-like interface, or only offer basic options, such as selecting between hierarchical and non-hierarchical paramers, etc.

title: just a thought: reordering confidence interval column positions
description:
It's a pet peeve of mine that when confidence intervals are asked for, `broom` returns a dataframe where the `estimates` are separated from their confidence intervals by few columns, which makes it a difficult visual task to assess the uncertainty associated with the estimates. 

This is much more difficult to decode
``` r
library(tidyverse)

broom::tidy(stats::lm(formula = wt ~ cyl, data = mtcars), conf.int = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 7
#>   term        estimate std.error statistic     p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)    0.565    0.401       1.41 0.169         -0.254     1.38 
#> 2 cyl            0.429    0.0623      6.88 0.000000122    0.302     0.556
```
than the following-
```r
broom::tidy(stats::lm(formula = wt ~ cyl, data = mtcars), conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, dplyr::everything())
#> # A tibble: 2 x 7
#>   term        estimate conf.low conf.high std.error statistic     p.value
#>   <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)    0.565   -0.254     1.38     0.401       1.41 0.169      
#> 2 cyl            0.429    0.302     0.556    0.0623      6.88 0.000000122
```

So I was wondering if you think it makes sense to reorder the columns in `broom` when confidence intervals are present in the output dataframe?

title: tidy.multinom() fails when formula is an object
description:
I usually assign formulae to a variable and refer to this variable in the model function. For lineare models (lm and glm) this works fine. However, using this approach with nnet::multinomial function raises an error: 

> Error in is.data.frame(data) : object '.x' not found

Here's a short reprex:

```r

# Assignin formula to a variable works with linear models
log_mod = vs ~ mpg + qsec + gear

mtcars %>%
  nest(-am) %>% 
  mutate(fit = map(data, ~ lm(log_mod, data = .x)),
         tidied = map(fit, tidy)) %>% 
  unnest(tidied)


# Same approach fails using nnet::multinom function
multinom_mod = cyl ~ mpg + qsec + gear

mtcars %>%
  nest(-am) %>% 
  mutate(fit = map(data, ~ nnet::multinom(multinom_mod, data = .x)),
         tidied = map(fit, tidy)) %>% 
  unnest(tidied)

# There's nothing wrong with formular or data, because defining the formular directly in multinom-function just works fine.
mtcars %>%
  nest(-am) %>% 
  mutate(fit = map(data, ~ nnet::multinom(cyl ~ mpg + qsec + gear, data = .x)),
         tidied = map(fit, augment)) %>% 
  unnest(tidied)
```
maybe this is a scoping issue?

title: Cleanup redundant @importFrom statements
broom for vars package on Vector Autoregressive Methods
description:
Thank you for such an awesome package.  I've been using it for the last month and really want to exploit all of its potential.  
In my last project I found an interesting example that I can't get my head around.  So I want to put it out there, and see if I can get help from the community.  

The package `vars` gives models for timed vectors.  Here are links for the [docs](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/vars/vars.pdf) and [vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/vars/vignettes/vars.pdf).  

The function `VAR` estimates models for the time-vector $y_t$ as follows:
$$ y_t = A_1 y_{t-1} + ... + A_p y_{t-p} $$    no LaTeX, =( 

But since $y_t$ contains several variables, its structure gets complicated. 

```
> library(vars)
> data("Canada")
> p1ct <- VAR(Canada, p=1, type="both")
> class(p1ct)
# "varest"
> names(p1ct)
# [1] "varresult"    "datamat"      "y"            "type"        
  [5] "p"            "K"            "obs"          "totobs"      
  [9] "restrictions" "call"  
```

The models are actually stored in `varresult` with the names of the variables. 

```
> class( p1ct$varresult$U )
# lm
> lm_U <- p1ct$varresult$U
```

For which I extracted the corresponding models in order to tidy them... and glance and augment them.  
There are two issues here: 
1. The main issue is that I couldn't get the fitted values back from the augmentation. 

```
compare_fitted <- cbind( lm_U$fitted.values, augment(lm_U)$.fitted )
compare_fitted
```
1. The second issue is minor.  When looking up about `augment`, I found that you can append the original data giving it as an argument.  In these models, the original data lost two rows because of the lagged observations.  So I got an error when I tried to recover it.  I was still able to get around it with `left_join` and `right_join`.  

In any case, my question is.  
a) How do the .fitted values get computed?  Would you know why I'm getting different ones?  
b) If I were to request methods for such `varest` class, or even better wanted to contribute in its development, how can I go about and do that?  I have been using R for a while, and am looking forward to taking the next step in contributing to a package.  

Cheers.

title: Compatibility with upcoming version of survival package
description:
Just got the follow revdep email

> The following packages all have a data() statement that fails, in their tests: aftgee, broom, flexsurv, frailtyEM, mlr3viz, muhaz, pammtools.  This is due to a change, namely that all the cancer data sets have now been bundled into a single file to save space and limit the CRAN "too large" complaints.   The data() command keys off the file name, not the data set name.   The help files for all the data sets have been updated.   Since survival lazyloads the data, I actually think you don't need a data() call, but I may be incorrect if survival is under 'imports' rather than 'depends'.

Not sure where the dev version of survival lives. If survival works on old R (say >= 3.3) we can bump the version dependency for `survival`. Otherwise we'll need to special case logic to handle the various survival versions.
